[h1]Summary:[/h1]
Five Dates is a ‘safe for work’ dating game that lets you play as Vinny, a somewhat customisable character who has just joined a dating app during those happy (not) days of COVID lockdowns, which saw an explosion in the trend of ‘video dating’. With some moderately funny, and some moderately sad scenes, this game does a good job at capturing the online dating scene during the lockdowns, and is perfect for the lonely introverts that enjoy the idea of staying up late talking to a romantic interest, but who have no idea where to start. 

[b]Reasons to Avoid:[/b]
- Panic scene may distress some viewers. 
- You can’t pick all five dates to start with, and the app forces eliminations.

[b]Reasons to Buy:[/b]
- Fair replay value.
- Easy to 100% achievements.
- Interesting diversity of characters among cast.
- Acting was very good. 
- Atmosphere of dating from home captured well.
- Choices felt fairly meaningful. 

[h1]Graphics:[/h1]
[b]Video:[/b]
The graphics in this game come down to the quality of the video footage. Some scenes look a little grainier than others, but this is an appreciated detail since we’re supposed to be video calling characters using laptops and phones, and people have different quality hardware. Some scenes are also shot in low light, for those evening dates, and this affects video quality too. 

Five Dates is not shot like a movie with cinematic shots – it is a camera pointed at someone’s face, like any video call. There’s nothing flashy to look at but it sets the scene well, and some date scenes actually had a lot of atmosphere despite this. It really was like getting a realistic glimpse into someone’s home – oftentimes cosy and intimate. I enjoyed it. 

[b]HUD:[/b]
User Interface elements were pleasingly minimal, only really appearing when in app menus, a progress tracking screen, or when you’re given a choice. The interface of the dating app looks professional and convincing, too. Some FMVs have quite awkward UI, but Five Dates felt well-done in this regard.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
If you’ve played these types of games before, it’s more of the same, but for those new to FMVs, they play out like movies that, at certain intervals, offer you interactive choices that ultimately give you control over which way the movie plays out. You don’t move characters like in normal videogames – the pre-recorded scenes have actors act out the choices you make. 

It’s probably quite a liberal use of the word ‘gameplay’, but it does have you interact with what’s happening on screen, which I’m very fond of. I often find movies can be a bit of a challenge precisely because they’re so passive – there’s little room for imagination unlike with books and there’s no room for interaction unlike with games. Well, FMVs are the answer to that second issue, if it’s one you resonate with. 

Five Dates presents choices quite nicely, I think. They don’t feel too fast and so you have time to think about your decision. Sometimes, characters will comment on/during the time it takes you to decide which I liked as an immersive way to allow you more time to think, without having to awkwardly freeze the video, or, like in other FMVs, force a choice for you so it can move to the next scene.

The fact there are choices at several intervals also gives the game good replay value, to both collect missed achievements (you cannot get them all in one playthrough) and to further explore the characters of the dates.

[h1]Story:[/h1]
[quote]Note: There is a mild panic scene where a character suffers from anxiety. More sensitive viewers may find this distressing.[/quote]

[b]Structure:[/b]
The story of this game is told in stages and as you move through each, a dating candidate is eliminated. You start by picking three dates and have your first call with each, then you pick two, then one. This in-game is explained as being the way the app works but it’s perhaps my biggest criticism of the game. Firstly, it necessitates more replays than are strictly necessary meaning that 100% completing the game takes longer, but somewhat artificially. Secondly, because it meant forcefully eliminating someone who you might have preferred to date. Sometimes you’re getting on well with two characters and it would be nice to be able to keep them both rather than just cut off someone who you were fond of. It feels a little bit cold – after all, it’s not like one of them couldn’t have remained a friend.

[b]You:[/b]
You can choose what sort of character you are, which affects your chances with the dates. Vinny can either be new to dating or have previous experience. You can pick his interests, zodiac, and career (broadly). Each of these corresponds better to some dates than others.

[b]Dates:[/b]
Dates respond differently to you depending on your choices too, which I liked as it gave them an authentic sense of weight, but very occasionally I’d make a choice and not expect a date to respond the way they did. One character particularly took me a few attempts to pass the first date with, and I’m not entirely sure why. We didn’t ‘click’, but I didn’t do anything ‘wrong’, either. 

This wasn’t a massively complex system and particularly where your interests, career, and zodiac are concerned, it never seemed to matter more than your choices which I was glad for. They had a soft effect on your compatibility but didn’t lock you out of any part of the game in my experience playing.

There are some moderately awkward scenes that while in no way offensive, do feel a bit cheesy, such as one where a video date must go to ‘clap for the NHS’ (something the UK started doing after Italy decided to honour their healthcare workers) which did feel a bit forced to me, but some might argue it was just an attempt to make the lockdown setting feel a bit more immersive. 

Most scenes were well-acted and convincing, though, and the story was enjoyable. Each date has quite a remarkably different character, and they’re played very well by their actresses. Even the characters I didn’t personally like were interesting, and I enjoyed replaying to see what they were like when you made it to the third date – how much of the thing(s) I disliked were really their nature, and how much was just a guard? I think for most, there is at least one character you’ll like, though it is interesting looking at the forums to see that my favourite is hardly mentioned by other users. If you find a character you click with, you can’t help but smile all the way through as you are invited to explore more of the character’s life and interests. 

[h1]Audio:[/h1]
The game audio was good. Some scenes sound like they were recorded on a phone in a kitchen because [i]they are recorded on a phone in a kitchen[/i] and that’s fine. It’s immersive in this game, in the context of video dates. It is subtle, but those who have careers more tech-orientated noticeably have better quality audio and video. I liked this small detail. 

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
Overall, Five Dates was an enjoyable FMV with fair replay value and easy enough achievements to 100% taking me about 7 hours. The characters were interesting, though not always likeable, but I feel there is someone there for most people, and when you find someone you like it elevates the game quite significantly. 

Small, immersive details like varying sound and video quality set the scene well but apart from the occasional mention of lockdown/NHS clap, you actually wouldn’t know this was set in the pandemic, so if you’re put off because you don’t want to be reminded of those bad years… I wouldn’t be. It’s not something you’re constantly reminded of. I’d recommend this game, particularly on sale – it’s good value against what you’d pay for a typical film.

This game is far better than I had expected.  Shockingly better.  The first thing I want to say is the acting is absolutely incredible.  I was expecting wooden characters with cliche interactions and back stories and that was not the case.  In fact, I completely bought everything the actors said.  These are serious actors and they deserve major kudos.

In terms of the game itself, it is really more of an interactive dating type simulator as opposed to a game, per se.  While it is not linear in nature (you can choose who you want to date, in what order), you are also somewhat limited in what you can say to them.  That is to be expected though, as you can only have so many options in a game like this.

For what it is, this game is incredible.   And it is wholesome too.  The dates feel like genuine first dates and everything that goes with them (the awkward nerves, the decision to drink or not, the break the ice games, etc) are done perfectly.

The only con with this game, and I'm stretching here, is that I felt that the first few dates ended a little more awkwardly than I would have expected.  I felt that maybe, and just maybe ,the game wanted to push me to have ambivalent feelings about the dates so that I'd be more open minded to the other girls.  I mean, wouldn't it be weird if you found the perfect girl on your first (virtual) date?  20 mins in, game over!

If you are on the fence about this game, I think you should give it a crack.  If nothing else, you will see some incredible acting and get to talk (kinda...) to some really attractive ladies.

[h3] What is it? [/h3]
[b] Five Dates [/b] is a FMV (full-motion video) game you can enjoy with minimal effort.
It simulates dating online via video dates in a fun, straightforward way.

You take on the role of Vinny, a 27 year old bachelor from London who is on the dating app for the first time. 

[h3] Stellar cast [/h3] 
The actors and actresses did a phenomenal job: Their acting is honestly better than [strike] some [/strike] a lot of shows on streaming services. 

The scenes flowed smoothly, and the chemistry in each scene was palpable, whether the two characters involved clicked or struck out! 

Kudos to the [i] Wales Interactive [/i] casting director(s) on their choices!

[h3] The gameplay [/h3]
It's been a while since I played a FMV so this was a very pleasant experience for me.

More so refreshing was the premise: Dating! More precisely dating exclusively online because of the quarantine way back when! Don't remind you, right? I know! *shudders*

There are little nods here and there to that time in our lives. It really made me appreciate that all that is well over and done with now.

The choices you make from the very start - like your interests (you may choose three from a long list), field of work, and even profile photo - do affect the course of the conversations later on.

You may notice the differences in outcome these bring only on another play through. You do need to pick the same dates but choose different responses to the same questions to experience these.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3033116118

I like how just like in real life, the way you handle yourself actually does affect the responses from your dates. For fun, try choosing responses you'd never go for in real life and enjoy the amusing responses!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3033115488

The game is structured in such a way that you need to be careful with your choices. [b] Five Dates [/b] actually offers an ethical way, if that's an apt description, to go about dating since it starts you off with three dates then after a date with each potential partner, it gradually narrows your options down to one. 
 
This is something I appreciate as I've dealt with [i] parallel daters [/i] myself before and I don't recommend that!

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3033116766

[h3] Graphics & Audio [/h3]
This is broadcast-level quality in terms of production. 
Crisp video with dreamy music - which you can enjoy listening to in the main menu only - a smart choice. 

[h3] Replayability & How long does one play through take? [/h3]
The game narrows your date choices from five to three from the get go, so if you'd like to experience all five dates, you'll need to play the game several times.

The good news is the game really delivers. I'll clarify: Even after I experienced all the dates more than once, played the game several times sometimes just for the fun of it, and unlocked all 15 achievements, the game still had a vast amount of video footage of interactions that I haven't seen yet. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3031586530

The TAB key allows you to quickly skip a video scene you've already watched in a previous play through. This makes replaying the game much faster.

If you skip almost all scenes you've already watched, you can do one full run in 30 minutes, give or take a couple of minutes. I played an extra run and timed it just to find this out.

[h3] Is there more? [/h3]
[b] Ten Dates [/b] is the sequel in which you play as a woman. 

I'm looking forward to playing it to see how [i] Wales Interactive [/i] made things look like from the opposite point of view! 

[h3] Conclusion [/h3]
Highly recommended, especially for couples or two strangers playing around with the idea! [b] Five Dates [/b] is in itself a great idea for a date!

Five Dates is a fun movie length Dating FMV with five girls you can go on three dates each with. The overall quality has a pretty good feel, the only thing that could have been better is the video quality itself at times especially darker parts get quite pixelated. Since this game literally is about video dating though I guess it makes sense that the camera quality isnt the best as a webcam also would not output the best picture. Apart from that it really felt quite high quality. I wrote that there is no skip, but I just didnt realize that there actually is a skip feature which is great.

Now the story itself is well actually exactly what you would expect it is really only dates and some dialogue with your friend. So after going on 5 dates you either end up being successfull or well failing to get the girl. Now the big positive is the dialogue and I have to say some of it is really quite good and definitely quite realistic at times and also very fitting with the entire covid situation. Some parts though are also quite awkward, those might also be intentional though to give more variety. Apart from those I really had a good time going through it and also had quite a few good laughs. 

I also like the variety of the girls as there should at least be one of them with a personality that you can appreciate. However since all the girls are quite specific and special that also makes you probably hate one or two of them, or at least dislike them. 

Overall a nice interactive movie you could say and the only thing I was missing was a nice ending cause it pretty much just ends after you finish the third date with the last girl. There is no Epilogue with how it develops after plus some actions of the girls are a bit weird. Apart from that a job well done and I would even say that the price aint that bad considering a movie ticket would be about the same price and I had more fun with this than many movies I watched in a cinema :D

[h1]⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Five Dates — Or: How I Spent Several Hours Judging Strangers Through My Monitor Like a Very Polite God[/h1]
Let me begin by saying this: Five Dates is not a game.
It is an interactive social experiment in which you are given control of a mildly anxious London man named Vinny and asked to navigate modern dating while the rest of us sit behind a screen, making life-altering romantic decisions with the same confidence we use to choose Netflix thumbnails.Which is to say: recklessly.

[b]The Premise (or: Speed Dating, But Make It Existential)[/b]
You are Vinny.
Vinny is single.
Vinny is on a dating app.
Vinny lives in London during lockdown.

Already this feels less like a game and more like a BBC documentary.

You’re presented with five potential dates, each beamed into your home via video call, which means the entire romance unfolds like a Zoom meeting where everyone remembered to put on trousers (mostly).

There are no swords.
No skill trees.
No loot boxes.

Your only weapons are:
+Tone of voice
+Facial expressions
+And the catastrophic power of saying the wrong thing about hobbies.

[b]Gameplay: Choose Your Own Social Disaster[/b]
Mechanically, the game is simple:
Person asks question.
You choose response.
Person reacts.
But emotionally? It’s like defusing a bomb while also trying to flirt.
Every dialogue choice feels weighted with the quiet terror of real life:
[h3]“Do I joke?”
“Do I be sincere?”
“Do I pretend I enjoy hiking?”[/h3]
One incorrect sentence and suddenly someone’s eyebrows go up in a way that says, Right. I will emotionally disengage now.
And that’s the genius of Five Dates.
It perfectly recreates the sensation of real dating, where one misplaced comment about pineapple on pizza can erase your entire romantic future.

[b]The Characters: A Carefully Curated Museum of Modern Humanity[/b]
Each date is lovingly crafted to represent a different flavour of human being.
You get:
+The confident one
+The awkward one
+The spiritual one
+The intense one
+The one who definitely owns crystals
They’re all charming in their own way, and also mildly alarming, like people you’d meet at a wedding and immediately start ranking in your head.

What’s impressive is how real they feel.
Not “Hollywood real.”
Actual real.
As in: they talk too much sometimes.
They overshare.
They have oddly specific opinions.
At one point I forgot I was playing a game and started mentally preparing polite exit strategies.

[b]Production Value: Surprisingly Not Awful[/b]
This is FMV (full motion video), which historically means “this will either be incredible or deeply cursed.”
Thankfully, Five Dates lands on the good side.
The acting is genuinely solid.
The writing is sharp.
The awkward pauses feel intentional rather than accidental.
Everyone behaves like actual people instead of walking romance tropes, which is refreshing in a genre usually powered by anime sighs and dramatic hair flips.
Also, special mention to Vinny’s facial expressions, which deserve their own BAFTA.
That man’s eyebrows do more emotional labour than most therapists.

[b]The Real Gameplay Loop: Self-Reflection[/b]
Here’s the unexpected twist:
You don’t just learn about the characters.
You learn about yourself.
Because at some point you realise:
-You are very conflict-avoidant.
-You panic when asked about future plans.
-You will absolutely choose “safe polite answer” over “honest personality.”
This game gently exposes your dating instincts like a psychological MRI.
By the end, I wasn’t sure whether I’d completed a romantic adventure or undergone a soft personality audit.

[b]Criticisms (Because I’m British and It’s Mandatory)[/b]
*Some conversations end just as they get interesting.
*A few branches feel shorter than expected.
*Occasionally you’ll wish you could say, “Actually, can I rewind that sentence from 30 seconds ago?”
But honestly?That’s dating.Real life also has terrible autosave.

[b]Final Verdict[/b]
Five Dates is clever, awkward, charming, and quietly brutal in how accurately it captures modern romance.
It’s not about winning.It’s about navigating vulnerability with a mouse.
You will cringe.
You will laugh.
You will accidentally ruin at least one promising relationship because you picked the wrong joke.
And somehow, you’ll enjoy all of it.

[h1]Five Dates[/h1]
[i]Emotional buffering[/i]

[b]Five Dates[/b] presents a unique concept that merges interactive storytelling with the world of modern dating apps, allowing players to navigate the complexities of romantic relationships from the comfort of their screens. While the game's innovative approach is commendable, it falls short of delivering a truly captivating experience, resulting in a middling affair.

[u][b]Pros[/b][/u]:

Fresh Concept: The game's premise of virtually dating five different characters through video calls is a refreshing take on interactive storytelling. It introduces an element of choice and consequence that adds depth to the narrative.

Timely Themes: Five Dates explores timely themes of modern dating, long-distance relationships, and the challenges of forging connections in a digital age. This relevance adds a layer of relatability to the characters and their struggles.

Character Depth: Each character has their own distinct personality and backstory, providing a sense of authenticity to their interactions. This variety ensures that no two playthroughs are exactly the same.

[u][b]Cons[/b][/u]:

Limited Gameplay: While the concept is intriguing, the gameplay mechanics remain relatively limited, mostly consisting of dialogue choices and occasional decision points. This simplicity can lead to a lack of engagement, especially for those seeking more interactive gameplay.

Shallow Relationships: Despite the efforts to establish meaningful connections, the virtual dating format inherently limits the depth of the relationships that players can build with the characters. The emotional impact can feel somewhat hollow as a result.

Uneven Storytelling: The quality of writing and character development varies between the different storylines. Some characters receive more attention and development than others, leading to an uneven storytelling experience.

Technical Limitations: The video call format, while innovative, occasionally suffers from technical glitches that can disrupt the immersion. Audio and video inconsistencies can break the flow of the conversations.

[u][b]Conclusion[/b][/u]:

Five Dates presents an innovative concept that attempts to merge interactive storytelling with the world of virtual dating. While the game's fresh approach and timely themes are commendable, it struggles to maintain a consistently engaging experience. Limited gameplay mechanics, shallow relationships, uneven storytelling, and occasional technical hiccups hinder its potential. While the game's exploration of modern dating dynamics might resonate with some players, its execution results in a lukewarm rating of 6/10. Those intrigued by the premise might find some enjoyment, but those seeking a more immersive and emotionally resonant experience may come away feeling somewhat unsatisfied.

[h1] 8/10 [/h1]

I've played several of the other games from Wales Interactive and came in with my expectations set at a certain level. The acting was consistently good throughout the game and the dialogue regularly made me laugh. 

So why don't I recommend this game after spending 4 hours to claim all the achievements?

Aside from it potentially not aging well after the lift of COVID-era lockdowns, I had no connection with the protagonist, Vinny. What's his actual backstory? Vinny's best friend was great at being supportive but gave me no insight into the character I was piloting. In one story, I was a vegan. In another, I was a meat eater. I had no idea whether my character was lying to everyone about everything or what he believed. It felt like, at times, *I* was supposed to choose what I wanted to do while other times were about what Vinny might want in order to "win" with the date.

Also, the lighting in the scenes was wildly inconsistent. It was distracting having a five-minute conversation where the background lighting would go from natural daylight to dark and back to bright daylight again with no explanation. There are a lot of scenes in this game, clearly filmed at different times of the day, but it broke immersion to see the sunlight changing so rapidly between portions of the same conversation.

"Five Dates" is a well-written mix of a Dating Sim and a Romantic Comedy story, which skillfully evades the plethora of clichés that have overwhelmed either genre. It's presented as a full-motion video game with frequent, meaningful choices for the player.

[h2]1. Story & Setting[/h2]
You play as Vinny, a 27-year-old male Londoner who has just joined a dating app. You have a few choices for "building" your character, with different profile pictures, day jobs, and hobbies, which all may affect details of the unfolding stories. Once you've created your Vinny, you can pick 3 women to date out of a total of 5 suggestions (these are always the same). After doing a first date with 3 of those, you can select up to 2 for a second date, and then one for a third date, though the women might decline if your previous date went badly. You'll also "debrief" your dates with a very supportive male buddy. The entire story takes place during the CoViD lockdown, so all conversations happen as video calls, no one ever meets in person.

The objective of the story is to win the heart of the woman you chose for your third date, and move the conversation from the dating app to a direct call. There is no overarching plot or mystery beyond this, though each of the women's stories has interesting details to explore. But this is absolutely not a mystery game, it's about having conversations with five (six if you count your buddy) well-written, believable people during online dates.

Each of the characters has their own distinct personality, with their own interests, strengths, and weaknesses. The script was written with good attention to detail, which gives the characters depth and doesn't fall into the terrible clichés that dating sims and romcoms often don't even try to get away from. It's also full of good-natured humor, harbors the occasional deep thought, and even contains some dating advice that would actually be useful in the real world. The conversations in this script are among the best-written I have ever seen in an FMV game.

It's noteworthy that the game can be approached in a number of different ways. Players can insert themselves into the main character, answer questions truthfully, and play it as a fairly realistic (though somewhat idealized) dating sim. Players can also try to "read" the characters, find out what each of the women is looking for, and try to "win" every girl's heart across several playthroughs. Players can also just explore the characters and their stories, and roleplay the protagonist (across several playthroughs) as very different characters. The game and its stories work fine either way, and the game doesn't judge (though if you behave like a jerk, then the women will let you feel that you're wasting their time).

Due to the lack of an overarching plot, the game is unfortunately very short - the first full playthrough takes about an hour, subsequent ones may be even shorter. You'll need at least five full playthroughs to complete every woman's story arc, and possibly a few more if you want to collect all the achievements (unless you managed to do that on the way). I spent about 6 hours exploring various paths until my experience felt reasonably complete, but even then, I've seen only about 500 out of 766 scenes.

[h2]2. Gameplay & Mechanics[/h2]
As typical for the genre, the mechanics are very simple: You see a short video clip, select between up to 5 choices for your response, see the next video clip with your conversation partner's response to your choice, and so on.

Player agency is fairly high compared to other games in the genre. Each of your choices usually elicits a specific, unique response (whereas other games often continue in the exact same way regardless of your choice, or just add a line or two depending on your choice). That said, each date has a fixed sequence of topics that it will usually circle back to, unless something goes really wrong. Your choices also influence how much your conversation partner likes you, and if you want, you can view that parameter as a percentage stat at any point in the game.

[h2]3. Graphics & Presentation[/h2]
There isn't much that can be said about the cinematography. The videos were filmed during lockdown and - as far as I understand - without a cameraman. Every actor was sent recording and sound equipment, and they then recorded their scenes themselves, mostly at home, presumably with guidance from the director. Thus there isn't anything visually spectacular in the videos, but they feel very authentic for a "person speaking into a webcam" scenario.

The acting was genuinely very good - really talented actors were given a well-written script and poured their hearts into it. Depicting believable, regular, "normal" people in a way that still captures the viewer's attention for an hour or longer is much more difficult than it sounds, but in "Five Dates", it worked exceptionally well for almost every single character. The conversations flow very naturally too.

The game doesn't use any special effects. Occasional background music accentuates particulary positive or detrimental choices, but never pushes into the foreground, so that is competently done.

[h2]4. Usability & Accessibility[/h2]
The game offers a single volume slider, a brightness slider, and a display mode toggle. A single language selector affects both the subtitles and the UI - some players would have preferred those functions separated, but there is very little UI text to begin with. Subtitles can be toggled on or off, and their size and contrast can be adjusted.

Two very important functions for FMV games are provided: One is a toggle for auto-pausing the game during decisions, instead of automatically taking one after a few seconds. Whether you want the increased tension of time pressure or rather play in a relaxed fashion, the game lets you do either. The other important function is the skipping of already viewed scenes - this makes repeated explorative playthroughs enjoyable, you won't have to spend an hour rewatching already-seen scenes just to find a handful of new ones.

The game saves automatically after every choice, but there is only one save state that keeps getting overwritten. The save state also tracks your statistics - scenes viewed, number of successful dates, etc.

[h2]5. Conclusion[/h2]
"Five Dates" is not a single story,  but rather a virtual interactive dating experience that provides many choices and varied responses. It combines a well-written script, interesting characters, and excellent acting into a very enjoyable package that's definitely worth a recommendation.

A game about dating but you are not the one actually getting the date but a somewhat preset character you can shape a bit. I bought this on a whim because reviews were positive and FMV games have been a rarity after the 90s with graphics becoming more and more realistic.

The actors and actress are actually pretty solid, it still somewhat feels scripted because each characters are pretty locked into a specific persona but it is to make the experience more interesting and there are a few twists. Having the best friends for a debriefing is actually a pretty good idea, it gives a break to the dating and usually brings some humour into the tray when the dates are not all rainbow and sunshine.

One playthrough is a bit short because it follow a 3-2-1 formula and you need multiple playthrough to experience the 5x3 amount of dates but the possibility of short sessions can be a nice thing if that's what you want. It feels like it ends a bit quickly after the third date, having something more after the dating could also be interesting, maybe a sequel? The full price is a bit high considering the length but it's a surprisingly enjoyable concept I would like more of.
I don't even care about the dates. Turk and J.D. just being BFFs is fun enough

Sometimes it's the shortest games that provide the most powerful, emotional, and authentic experiences. If you make honest choices (for better or for worse) then you will get genuine results. The winning isn't in scoring 100% with every date by giving fake answers, the winning is in landing the outcome that feels right to you.

The acting is phenomenal; I really felt like I was guiding someone through actual video dates. It was exciting, fun, and sometimes moving.

It's not surprising so many gamers would give bad reviews... being gamers and all.

If you have any heart and humanity to you, you'll probably enjoy this. If you think the point of dating is to score no matter what... well, you might be disappointed.

"The Complex" is a medium-length (about 80 minutes) interactive thriller movie about two scientists and an intern, who try to disentangle a web of corruption while being trapped in a high-security lab. The two scientists have a prior history together and the intern, whose motives are in question, has been infected with deadly nanocells that ravage her body.

I found the story interesting and enjoyable, though some parts are a bit far-fetched, and in one of the paths, it needlessly spins into violence that feels tacked-on just to have some action in the movie. The acting was okay - nothing stellar, but it got the job done, and especially the complicated relation of the two main characters was presented very well.

The occasional choices were engaging, and the game tracks how well the other characters think of you, which means that the same choice can lead to different outcomes depending on how your previous choices affected your relationship with that character. This is a fresh technique that enhances immersion and replayability. That said, the story is still too linear for my taste - it follows the exact same plot with just a few additions or omissions based on your choices, and around the middle it branches into two different paths, that's it. Rhinotales' "She Sees Red" did a better job in that regard.

There are nine different endings, and exploring them is fun because contrary to Wales Interactives's previous games in this genre, this one lets you skip scenes that you have already seen. This turns hunting for achievements and/or different endings into an engaging experience, rather than the tedium of previous titles. Some of the endings feature surprises, and watching all of them gives you a better understanding of the plot, though once again "She Sees Red" showed that this can be done even better.

The game does not have any puzzles to speak of, unless you regard "finding a good ending" as one. I didn't miss them since your choices are still interesting and meaningful, they just focus more on handling personal relations and finding the right tone, rather than traditional problem-solving.

Altogether, "The Complex" is still not quite where I would like interactive movies to be, but it is a noticeable improvement over the company's previous titles like "Late Shift" and "The Bunker", especially in terms of user-friendliness. It's a bit pricey considering that there's little reason to spend more than 4 hours with it even as a completionist, but filming movies isn't cheap, and I prefer an engaging 4-hour experience over a boring, drawn-out longer one.

One final note that wasn't important enough to mention earlier: the game is pretty amateurish in its presentation of medical procedure. The scientists handle the intern's cannula without disinfection, they leave blood spittle on reused equipment (that also does not get disinfected), and if you have some knowledge of these things, be prepared that this game does worse than even a bad TV show in that regard. These are minor details that didn't affect my personal enjoyment, but they are noticeable enough to potentially be an immersion breaker for some players.

I was willing to give this a recommendation if it wasn't for the inaccurate "choices matter" tag. Almost none of your choices matter. A singular somewhat arbitrary choice near the end completely dictates your ending between two primary endings, everything else being small variations on those endings. There's maybe one of those variations that could be called a seperate ending, so that's three endings. And only one of the characters matter for some of the variation in ONE of the primary endings. If you want a okay FMV story, then this is for you, but if you want your choices to matter, look elsewhere.

I was excited to play The Complex, expecting a tense interactive thriller, but the storytelling was unfortunately very weak and it does little to create enthusiasm to see the alternate paths after your first playthrough. The sequence of events, which doesn't change all that much except near the final minutes, takes rather cheap shortcuts and paints characters in such broad strokes that it feels as though it was made from a thin, bullet-point outline rather than a properly fleshed out screenplay. I don't want to get into spoilers, but the security of this supposedly very new, "spared no expense" superlab somewhere near London is laughably bad and the nature of the bio threat, while gross and painful in its visible symptoms, doesn't make much (if any) sense.

Things are somewhat better on the technical side. The video quality is decent, I would guess 1080p, and looked fine on my 4K screen. Not a blu-ray level bitrate, but good enough. The decision prompts also have a nice, clean design. However, one glaring issue is the music, which seems to be hard-embedded into the videos themselves, and this creates situations of both abrupt fade outs of the score and moments that last longer than they should where I've made a plot decision but the lead character (supposedly an expert research scientist) stands in place looking indecisive, often spoiling the drama of the moment.

There was a great deal of potential here, I love smart science fiction stories like The Andromeda Strain, and Wales Interactive really impressed me with their earlier FMV game Late Shift, where your decisions can lead to wildly different outcomes, but the designers here made major errors not giving the story and fluidity of the experience the attention they deserved.

[h1]Story[/h1]
After treating the victims of a bio-weapon attack in the oppressive state of Kindar, the head scientist in Nanocell technology, Dr Amy Tenant is confronted with a possible new outbreak in London. Reports of a Kindarian citizen vomiting blood on a local subway lead to terrorism suspicions and Amy, along with other colleagues quickly find themselves under lockdown in their laboratory. Racing against time, they try and uncover the identity of their assailants as well as the truth about their organisation and what really happened on Kindar.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The Complex is similar to an interactive movie, like Netflix's 'Bandersnatch'. It mostly involves watching the scenes unfold on screen and occasionally making a decision. These choices are supposed to be the backbone of the game and encourage players that all decisions matter and influence character traits, endings and other relationships. Regrettably, I found this was not entirely correct and most choices, leading up to the final chapters were completely null, and had little to no effect on the story.

Sometimes, after making a decision, another character would step up and say that's the wrong choice and the game will automatically proceed with the latter selection, making the entire 'choice' process completely null. 
The menu screen does easily display how many scenes have been unlocked, acting as motivation to encourage players to replay and complete to 100%. Yet, even after picking other options, the exact same cutscenes would play time after time and I found myself continuously pressing tab until I finally got to a new screen. This process also becomes more apparent after each replay and soon becomes tiresome. Although I was fascinated with my first playthrough and found the story quite compelling, I was also under the impression that the gameplay was tailored to my own decisions, which I later subsequently found out, that this wasn’t completely true.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2044605236

Nonetheless, some of the endings are different and took me by surprise, but instead of being influenced by a multitude of selections throughout the game, I found it was only really impacted by a few key options towards the end. To give a better understanding of the game length, I achieved 5/9 endings in only 2.5 hours, with the first full playthrough only averaging around 85 minutes. Before purchasing, it is important to note that this is not a long game, like many others in the genre and can be completed to 100% in one sitting quite easily. 

 [h1]Graphics + Sound[/h1]
Being an FMV game, the graphics and sound are of course, decent with high quality filming and it does not appear restricted through low-budgets or other restraints. The acting is excellent and manages to avoid the cringe factor from dramatized expressions and responses, which I have seen plague many other FMV titles.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
The Complex is a great, interactive cinematic experience for sci-fi fans as well as FMV enthusiasts. Its compelling story and well directed script make for an enjoyable first playthrough. However, choices in subsequent re-runs feature majority of the cutscenes that players have already seen, highlighting the low importance our choices actually have over the story. Some of the endings do make replaying a tad more encouraging, but to know that they are only swayed by key decisions, making earlier choices seemingly null, frankly is just disappointing and I advise on waiting for a sale before purchasing.

The Complex is an FMV game about a virus outbreak in London. The main character Dr Amy Tenant is a scientist who is trapped in a laboratory with a few colleagues, and must find a way to escape.

This is basically an interactive movie, so gameplay involves watching the video scenes and then occasionally making a choice to influence how the story plays out.

My first playthrough took only 76 minutes to complete, and my 2.6 hours playing time represents two full playthroughs. The actors did a good job, but the quality of the story is limited by its short length.

While there are eight different endings, most of the story will play out in a very similar way. During my second playthrough I made a few different choices and I saw a couple of new scenes, but then the story moved itself back onto the main path to continue playing out the same way. I also counted three occasions where I could choose between two options, I chose option B, but another character overruled me and did option A anyway.

I bought The Complex as part of a bundle. I specifically wanted Dead Reset, but I saw that for an extra £2 I could get 2 more games including this one. So the best recommendation I could give for The Complex is that I wouldn’t buy this game by itself, but its worth playing if you pick it up in a bundle.

我从纯玩家角度出发（毕竟是外行），坦白说，玩之前我的期待可能有点高了。但事实确实是我玩的时候是带了些失望的。影游与我个人而言，仍然只是带有轻量交互的影视剧作品。他仍然是游戏，但是质量我认为主要体现在这几个方面：
1. 剧情本身的设计
2. 演员的演技表现
3. 作品的剪辑呈现
4. 作为游戏的可交互性表达（乐趣）
5. 内容体量的丰富性。
分别对应了 剧情（1）、制作（2、3）、乐趣（4、5）

但是这部作品对我而言：
1. 剧情本身的设计没有特别出彩的地方（没有超出预期的剧情逻辑、没有深刻的人物刻画、没有宏大的世界背景（这题材限制也正常））
2. 制作上，演员本身的演技只能说是还不错，是我目前认为最优秀的一点；而叙述剪辑上，我不确定是沟通问题亦或是导演水平不足，我始终觉得整个故事都带有很多瑕疵，我几乎看不下去（逻辑漏洞、剧情衔接突兀、叙事铺陈不够等）
3. 乐趣方面，基本上就是简单的qte吧，没有什么可指摘的，也没有什么可记忆的，而体量更是短小精悍，我3小时就通关了，一共也就进了4次失败结局。
基于以上的体验，我又怎么可能说去安利给我那几乎没听说过影游的朋友，就算是玩影游的朋友我的评价也称不上是良好。这种情况下，我认为这部作品虽然确实不差，但是想破圈也没什么可能吧？
玩到最后我的感觉甚至是说不定拍成短剧效果会更好？？

题材方面确实很有自己的思考，但是可能也缺乏对市场的充分调研感觉？这个题材太过严肃，我不认为是在有充分底气之间比较适合做的题材。对于制作组的精神我很认可，但我却无法认同。

以上均是我个人看法，缺乏专业知识，所以很多地方可能也看的很狭隘，但这都是我内心的声音，仅供参考。

最后，仍然希望制作组的所有人，保持初心，不断前行。即使是失败，也是一次有意义的失败。做过总比不做强。我仍然期待看到各位成功的那天！不管是在哪个赛道、哪个行业、哪个领域，都祝大家未来心想事成。:LIS_pixel_heart:

神人一般的抽象剧情，让人不忍思考编剧的文化水平，就是女主一路爽杀，既无游戏性也无观赏性，还有我们经典的[spoiler]按着玩家的头宽恕霸凌者的[/spoiler]神秘剧情。而且到头来并不是跟所谓霸凌有关，无非是个爽文复仇小故事罢了。

一部让人哭笑不得的闹剧，剧本为了悬疑而悬疑，剧情为了砂仁而砂仁，题材为了霸凌而霸凌，悬疑影游的每一个要素都占了，但是每一项都如空中楼阁一般，剧本建立在一个空气做的地基上，这是一部和现实完全脱节的，反映霸凌现象的非现实题材互动影游。
值得肯定的是，这部互动影游有一定自知之明，中不中日不日的洋泾浜行为，可以用来解释这是日本的华侨学校，进而将这部剧诸多不可能发生的事件，归结于这里既不算传统意义上的日本，也不是大陆，可以规避一些较为麻烦的审查和解释一下浅显的逻辑漏洞。但是作为一个在人类社会发生的事件，还是不能规避这部剧过于离谱的设定和剧情。董事长李启铭，作为校董，一位有权有势的BOSS，为什么在有一堆目击者的情况下主动把自己的软肋端到这些人眼前，在不是自己第一个致女主姐姐受伤的情况下，在女儿还没有铸成杀人大错的情况下，强行捅了女主姐姐一刀（如果不捅，这部互动电影不成立）但是作为一个有权有势的人，这种人会这么轻易的授人以柄，实在让人百思不得其解。而且剧情中期铺垫李启铭有权有势，阴险狡猾，结局轻易就被女主设计绑架，完成了复仇，也足够敷衍。
剧情中李启铭的反常只能理解为作为校董的他患有精神分裂，所以在对自己有百害而无一利的情况下，给女主姐姐来了这么一刀，然后看了结尾的我们知道，有收藏癖的李启铭最后把女主姐姐的尸骨转移到自己宅基地，方便以后东窗事发，警察能在第一时间联想到谁是凶手。
看这部互动影游不能过脑子，一旦过了脑子就会发现导演和编剧把所有观众都当成了智障。但是这部影游又搞了这些悬疑感，有那么一点杀人魔王金田一，一集屠一群人的感觉，只不过，看少年金田一，观众看完一集，了解到真相会有复仇的爽感，看这部互动影游，观众看完完全没有什么复仇的爽感，因为开挂了的，人见人爱的女主，杀的的要么是精神病要么是低智人。
初次了解这款游戏是在小黑盒，所谓的解散公告里，得知这部游戏刚发售就要解散，而且制作人不吝溢美之词，在介绍这款游戏时用了瑕不掩瑜，T1级别，问心无愧等话语，那篇公告当即就引起了我的好奇和惋惜。直到这部影游的片尾字幕结束后，我终于从眼前一黑，如坐针毡，变成了啼笑皆非，无可奈何的大彻大悟之中，我终于明白《牛来》这样一部神片为什么能赢得市场，毕竟怎么样都是输，我上我也行，至少能让观众自己为自己加冕，而不是陷入素不相识的人的自我感动。
剧情无聊的一批 互动选项能再弱智点？

妹妹为了姐姐孤身一人潜入校园，妹妹为了意外横死的姐姐，妹妹竟然设计一连报复了五个人，那五个人曾经向姐姐捅刀子，妹妹帮姐姐报仇成功了，妹妹好端端的“读完书”成功的在校园里混到毕业了。我觉得，游戏有时候真的只是游戏。现实生活里，如果一个人为了自己一条亲人的命，以“报仇”为理由害死了不止一条命，其实是很滑稽的。因为，不是每一条命都重要的。不是所有角色都有同样多的戏份的。游戏里的妹妹只是害的很多角色提早退场了。妹妹你会委屈，难道别人不会委屈？妹妹你与别人的生活不同，别人觉得委屈的那种情绪的点，妹妹你不懂的。妹妹你这样子“报仇”了，妹妹啊，妹妹你只是很奇怪的把你姐姐的退场模式复制到了其他人的命运里。妹妹你不是在“报仇”吧，妹妹你只是在“扩散”吧。游戏真是有些幼稚了。（举例：江山北望里面的司空氏做到了诗句里写的”王师北定中原日，家祭无忘告乃翁“，他们司空一族达成了九州同。他们古风游戏都能制作的相当成熟稍显幼稚，你们校园游戏怎么就是很稚嫩？）

很少给差评，但这次是真绷不住了，看到制作组的解散公告（看口吻，发布那篇文章应该是个人行为）更绷不住了
他原文说什么呢？“画面质感不重要”，“讲好故事最重要”，结果因为“成本控制”，“多结局变成两个结局”，又说“勘景不顺利”，所以“双结局变成单结局+一个名存实亡的阉割‘结局’”
我就没见过几个画面质感差但剧情好的影游，好的剧本不会随便献身给一个用iPhone拍摄的剧组
游戏本身也是很粗糙，可以说是平铺直叙的犯罪叙事。以往玩推理游戏、犯罪游戏，有点漏洞我都不会太苛刻，因为我知道哪有天衣无缝的事呢，况且就是个游戏不用太认真，但这回的漏洞也太大了，这校董一直帮主角掩盖杀了四五个人的犯罪事实就是为了借刀杀人把最后的校长除了？换校长意义不明，就算换校长真的有什么让你集团董事长求之不得的利益，私立学校校董换校长不是有很多方法吗？从一开始就预判一个陌生人的行为（甚至知道这个陌生人的存在都很牵强），甚至在抽血检查之前就预判了，于是帮忙掩盖犯罪踪迹？童话故事都不会这么编
流程短 剧情差 真的导演水平巨差 题材说是校园霸凌 就i是个复仇的题材 不知道跟校园霸凌有什么关系
恶心到了，孔鸢不救还不行，快死去吧，她凭什么被救，霸凌别人，说别人的死是她好起来的开始，麻痹 国产剧看多了？包饺子是吧。恶毒霸凌女的人设，还他妈的能被原谅，纯搞笑。

……做的一言难尽,为了过审?强行替换成日本,导致剧情完全不对应了,反而矛盾增加太多了.
甚至制作的部分也有很多粗心大意的地方(耳机带反了就没发现吗).
并且部分剧情"怪力乱神"你们是碟中谍吗技术这么高超.

这年头影游都是这样前期打广告,剧情内容随便做,发售就刷好评.
一手好牌打得稀烂。看别人玩儿了第一章买的游戏 结果发现就第一章最好。 那么多好演员上镜那么少 演得好的戏份少 除了主演演的都很好。剧情一般 和同期的鬼才没法比。 6分是给除了女主角以外的其他演员 6/10
第一章就玩出了个死局，然后就没办法继续下去，也没办法从头开始，这什么意思？才开始了20分钟，这就结束了？果断退款

“我将会一一回报”


前言：这是我全探索的第129部互动影游，心心念念很久的作品，题材，人设，故事背景，音乐品味等等都是跟我非常非常的对味，一直都想玩，这部真的是我期待很久的作品，不是什么大作，但是我本人曾经吹过它可能是“年度黑马”，今天就让我们来看看什么个事……（音乐品味是真的很不错，深得我心！）现在打完了，我只能说……有点失望，因为它给我的最美好的憧憬全都在DEMO里了……（其实当初DEMO就发现有点不对劲，开头两个女死得太快了）跟我预期的那种复仇题材好片相差甚远（本身我是觉得哪怕不至于超越“罪金”和“园区”，也应起码差不多），总分：3.5,3分给还算流畅，不过不失的剧情，0.5给选题。

个人颜值排名：1，樱井芳子；2，李曼婷；3，孔鸢；4，张瑶=纪晴天/顾盼晴；5，顾盼雨；6，陆雪

说两句题外话，不喜勿喷，我觉得女主有某种角度有点像朱朱诶……张瑶我在最初玩DEMO的时候其实觉得她挺漂亮的，挺喜欢的，但是当我后来见过她在《主角》的形态之后……祛魅了，个人观点而已，我的审美不代表您的品味，互相理解，互相尊重

个人喜爱度：1，女主；2，孔鸢

我就喜欢这种有仇必报，直来直去的性格，孔鸢这种狠人性格也不错。

最有气质：樱井芳子

最美场景：如果不是这一幕，那也就没有了。


UI&程序：
美术风格，主界面是时下流行的影游常规模版样式，主界面应该是一张AI动图循环，设计特点是每当网球进球筐推车的时候都会发出撞击声，设置，章节选择以及故事线页面没什么好说的，就是规规矩矩，深色暗黑风打底，没有太特别的地方，故事线比较简单（但触发条件不简单），至于资料馆的界面有点像曾经的“天命重启”初版的线索界面。

BGM非常好听，今年最好听的影游BGM了，尤其主界面那首，制作人的品味不错，音乐再次上大分。

直接进入“老生常谈”环节：有完美跳过；有窗口模式（但是固定调整分辨率改变大小那种模式）；有多国语言（非常多）；有做鼠标UI；有按键说明（说明里没有跳过，但亲测依然是“Q”）；树状图里有放大缩小滚轮（不过是前后的）；有探索度进度数值显示，但不是条；有档案室；有排行榜。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

缺点：
1，设置里“页面音量”描述有误，其实那个是音效的音量，不是背景音乐的音量。

2，DEMO存档不继承

“老生常谈”环节：有视频音量和音效的大小调节，但没有总音量和背景音量的调节；没有快速定位；没有内置成就系统；没有开关字幕功能。

备注：

1，本作没有关闭男主语音不属于缺点，首先人家就没有男主。

2，本作没有拍照功能不属于缺点，我一向认为非恋游和擦游不是十分需要这个功能。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

特色功能：
1，推理型玩法。


2，某些探索场景设置了限时搜索时限。


3，“故事墙”，就是“13号房”和“情反游戏”都用过的功能，算是制作组的精神延续了，可惜的是这次的体验没有前面提到两部作品那么好，它是类似于通过和官网建立超链接的形式，然后引导用户去官网上留言，那自然就没有以前的在客户端上的体验感好了。

（冷知识：官方，游影互娱公司的创始股东团队中有经典游戏“13号房”曾经的主创成员之一，所以本作中涉及大家大量熟悉的元素，现在所有问题都阔然开朗了。）


4，哇塞！影游稀有的外国语配音（但我不确定是不是AI语音还是人声）


5，这两个字面意思，列举出来只是因为并不是每一部作品都会有。


6，拿钥匙小游戏，是不是有种似曾相识的感觉呢？哈哈，像极了张扬躲避巡逻宿舍的卫兵时的那个逻辑，不过这个明显简单很多。



7，这个小游戏跟之前“99”里面的如出一撤。


8，加一个“喜闻乐见”的功能，我说为什么排行榜没人投票的呢……原来如此。


剧情&演技：
演技没什么好说的，非常自然的一部作品，所有人演技均不尬，流畅，自然，舒服，并非特指老戏骨，连那几个年轻演员都很自然，专业，因此并没有什么可以说的，就一点不知道为什么部分配角或不重要角色的配音总有一股译制片的味道，很多配角听上去都不像是自己的声音。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

按照惯例，都是问题和吐槽：
1，吕三PC到底为什么要打扮呢？没必要啊……

2，穿帮情节：众所周知日本上牌上路的汽车都是右舵的（并不是众所周知），然而本作中汽车全是左舵，我当然知道不可能真去日本拍，但是穿帮我就指出来。

3女主根本找不到吕三的另外一个窃听器到底放在孔校长办公室的哪里，请问她后面又是怎么用那个窃听器来听反派们讲话的呢？

4，这是一个“龙国”已经统治世界的平行时空吗？所有人都说中文，每次电视台新闻出现的时候主标题都是汉字，副标题才是日文，新闻内容都是汉字……

5，直到全探索都没有稍微认真的讲解过一下那个杀掉孔校长的神秘男（大概率是李启铭手下）的介绍。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

最有恋爱感情节：本作没有恋爱剧情，所以没有恋爱感一说，所以这个板块这次将替代成作者对本作情感部份的感概（没错，作者说的是我，不是主创）

第五章结尾彩蛋，张茂枫写信给妹妹张瑶那一段……莫名的有种唏嘘感和辛酸感，虽然他是反派，但这样能从人物内心深处各种角度去刻画角色，并且能让读者有感受的，才是好作品。

趣点：
1，一开始那个鼠标左键连点的主角姐姐的qte是无论如何都赢不了的？

2，说个题外话，既然是以日本为背景的故事，为什么连俄语语音都有了，日语没有呢？

3，说个场外话，与游戏无关，只是我觉得一切缘分都是这么的奇妙，14号发售的这两部作品共同点很多，大家主创都是曾经的著名IP里面的参与者走出来的，而且两家都是广州的公司，最神奇的莫过于本来“鬼才”是19号发售，现在换成了14号，这就是命运~！！（哈哈，我相信一定有兄弟懂我这个梗……）

4，2027的日本已经有这样的AI眼镜了吗？牛逼啊！


5，哈哈，懂？芳子这么聪明，进去起码是梦娜的左右手吧？


6，哈哈哈哈哈，懂的都懂，再次致敬“杨校长”梗，这个彩蛋在第六章“杨校长”……我说的是孔校长的房间搜证节点里，点击隐藏的保险箱触发。


谁是真女主：哈哈，你们说呢？好难猜哦~~哈哈。

档案：档案里面有角色的各种剧照，好消息！可以下载，并且还可以自选路径！然后其余的是角色的时间线和一些彩蛋视频，以及隐藏视频。

纪晴天：纪晴天的第三段视频是隐藏剧情，内容是第六章之后第七章之前的她们三人的一段陆雪老师帮她们两个补习学业的日常欢乐剧情。

樱井芳子：冷知识：1，仁波切，藏语音译，藏传佛教里，认证转世活佛，成就极高的高僧尊称。2，单道人为错误写法，正确是丹道人，主修内丹功法的道人。3，望川寺，真实存在，不过是在我国云南昆明啸狮山。

孔玉书：为什么没有早年申请创办“戒网学校”的经历记录的？哈哈哈哈……

以上就这么多，其余的档案个人认为没有什么有价值信息或有趣的地方就不作盘点了。

标题解释：这是一句纪晴天也就是顾盼晴在游戏里的台词，你就当我纯碎想不到有什么好的标题，随手拿来用的吧，但是……其实挺贴合剧情的，“我将会一一回报~~~！！”

总结：整体流程有点短，而且节奏进行得实在有点快，题材上是“复仇类”类型片，本质是比隔壁“鬼才”有着天然上的优势，有趣很多，但无奈你体量太短，比人家恋游还短……然后跟自己的“精神前作”（“13号房”）比，就更加……那可是神作殿堂范围级别的作品啊。题材和拍摄都非常不错，有巨大的吸引力，但实机游玩过程播片过多，交互不足，分支和互动玩法做得不够好，严重单线，比制作组自己的前作“99”差天共地，“99”的剧情一般，但是游戏性可是很好的……

有很多无效选项，也就是那种遇见一个人然后问他几个问题，然后几个问题都可以问完，没有对错，并且一定要问完才可以进入下一段剧情那种，那倒不如直接播片？这种情况很多作品都有出现，甚至“隐守”……，然后搜证环节有点多，其实搜证环节就是等于面对物品（非人类）时的这种“硬选环节”……

日本角色依然用中文说话有点出戏，樱井我们可以理解成她在华侨学校上班必须会中文，但是其他的角色呢？院长，其他日本警察，那些就没有必须要会中文的理由了，如果换成像“天命”或者“上川”那样，该说日语的说日语，该说国语的说国语那样就好多了。

全程叙事节奏过快，一个个BOSS死得太快，不是不可以一章干掉一个，可以的绝对，看看“情反”一样的架构，一章节打一个干部，但是，人家每一章有充足的铺垫，精彩的斗智斗勇，跟反派的心里博弈，氛围张力拉满，而且还有多分支，多互动，并且前面的每一个章节也将和后面的章节产生蝴蝶效应联动，但本作每章其短，然后依旧一章干掉一个，我都没来得及感受（说白了就是打他我都没有实感，不爽）就结束了，“杨校长”死得糊里糊涂，本身我就是因为“杨校长”再度复出影游，而且制作组是“13号房”主创成员之一，然后题材还是经典的类型片，复仇题材，所以我曾经夸下海口，“年度黑马”，但现在自打嘴巴，除了题材方向好，还有整个流程剧情还算通顺以外，其他的可以说是跟我当初的期望值拉大了一个非常大的反差值，跟主创的前作，神作“13号房”无法比拟，这么说吧，“恶校”跟“13号房”之间的距离可能是差了1.5个“上川”到“隐守”的距离……因为“上川”起码虽然没有剧情厚度，但好歹有个长度，然后在游戏性和互动玩法上极其出色。

结尾，最终BOSS草草收场，显得匆忙之余还把李启铭前期的人设破坏，严重降智了，最后庆幸的一点是在STEAM平台发行，所以最终女主们没有被“黑底白字”ZZZQ。（然而彩蛋里也没逃过一劫，哈哈）

非常精彩的一点是，当我们走“邪道线”，把女主纪晴天杀死之后，主角可以切换成孔鸢继续游戏，秒啊！通过这条线我们可以得知，李曼婷原来不是女主杀死的，她真正的死因是被她爸李启铭杀死……可惜的是这条线并没有延续下去，就到这戛然而止了，如果是真的可以切换主角，然后延续到第七章，最后还有一条真正的大分支，再搞个黑暗结局，那高低得再加0.5分，现在这个不是真正的“邪道线”。

冷知识：一，根据日本永山九大量刑标准，日本审判非常看重动机正当性，被害人过错等因素，死者本身存在重大过错，凶手以复仇为动机杀害被害人会大幅降低主观恶性，加之女主为高中生，所以极大可能会被判处12-18年有期徒刑，反正低于20年（日本有期刑期封顶20年），并且之后可以假释，被判死刑的可能性极低。

二，日本本身是一个很难会被量刑死刑的国家，说个这次应该真的是众所周知的事件，2022年当众枪杀前首相的凶手山上彻也最终被判无期，所以女主几乎是100%不会死刑，并且加上上面各种因素和条件，还有后期良好表现，10+左右，最终会被放出社会。

---


关于难度，如果你不100%探索，只要求单线通关，这是个短小而精致的游戏，很容易，但如果想要全成就，全探索那它将非常难……

1，第一章的这个探索场景，这里有一个隐藏的搜证，一定要点击这里，界面没有展示出来，虽然这个证据后面章节也会出现，但是这样你第一章的探索度收集也会影响，所以这里必须点击这个图中的位置，同一个位置，这里要解锁下面那条线必须等到搜证时间结束。（这也是“13号房”的经典玩法了）



2，第二章“完美犯罪”上面那个节点需要把孔鸢的怀疑度拉满，然后到这才能触发，一般很少人在没有提示的情况下会全选了提升怀疑度的选项。


3，第三章的这个节点的解锁跟第二章的“自己解锁”还是拿“备用钥匙”有关。


4，第四章这个“车前闹剧”节点的上下线，跟第一点有没有发现那个隐藏搜证有关，有发现和没发现是分别不同的线。


5，第五章“成功上车”这个节点上面这条死亡结局线需要在第四章“白露窃听”节点QTE失败，被张警官看见。

关于推介与否，首先一个很重要的问题，就是大家有没有制作组前作《与美女合租的99种死法》？如果没有的话，闭眼入，因为本作制作组有一个很牛的骚操作，首发即捆绑，而且绑的还是自家作品，30块可以入两部作品，平均值15块一个游戏，而且都是3.5分或以上的作品，这价钱根本就不需要吹，只需要通知就行了，这性价比大家都知道怎么选，但如果你是已经拥有了“99”的用户，则可以26购入本作，价钱其实也不算贵，但这就看你对题材的喜爱程度了。

最后，这次博主终于能抽出时间能在“绍宋”上之前可以把“都要”完成了，然后打完之后想休息一下，最近太累了，好累……我知道今天是“重生2DEMO”上线的日子，但是我不打算去玩了，我知道它很有趣，我不管是演员还是游戏本身的质量都很吸引我，但是我本人一向不太喜欢玩DEMO，因为打完了，后面正式版出来存档不继承又得再打一遍，而且让我看完第一章，非常好奇了，吊着瘾却要等几个月才能玩到全部剧情……这种感受不想在尝试了，除非闲得发慌，感谢兄弟们又一次看了那么久废话了，下次再会！

我从纯玩家角度出发（毕竟是外行），坦白说，玩之前我的期待可能有点高了。但事实确实是我玩的时候是带了些失望的。影游与我个人而言，仍然只是带有轻量交互的影视剧作品。他仍然是游戏，但是质量我认为主要体现在这几个方面：
1. 剧情本身的设计
2. 演员的演技表现
3. 作品的剪辑呈现
4. 作为游戏的可交互性表达（乐趣）
5. 内容体量的丰富性。
分别对应了 剧情（1）、制作（2、3）、乐趣（4、5）

但是这部作品对我而言：
1. 剧情本身的设计没有特别出彩的地方（没有超出预期的剧情逻辑、没有深刻的人物刻画、没有宏大的世界背景（这题材限制也正常））
2. 制作上，演员本身的演技只能说是还不错，是我目前认为最优秀的一点；而叙述剪辑上，我不确定是沟通问题亦或是导演水平不足，我始终觉得整个故事都带有很多瑕疵，我几乎看不下去（逻辑漏洞、剧情衔接突兀、叙事铺陈不够等）
3. 乐趣方面，基本上就是简单的qte吧，没有什么可指摘的，也没有什么可记忆的，而体量更是短小精悍，我3小时就通关了，一共也就进了4次失败结局。
基于以上的体验，我又怎么可能说去安利给我那几乎没听说过影游的朋友，就算是玩影游的朋友我的评价也称不上是良好。这种情况下，我认为这部作品虽然确实不差，但是想破圈也没什么可能吧？
玩到最后我的感觉甚至是说不定拍成短剧效果会更好？？

题材方面确实很有自己的思考，但是可能也缺乏对市场的充分调研感觉？这个题材太过严肃，我不认为是在有充分底气之间比较适合做的题材。对于制作组的精神我很认可，但我却无法认同。

以上均是我个人看法，缺乏专业知识，所以很多地方可能也看的很狭隘，但这都是我内心的声音，仅供参考。

最后，仍然希望制作组的所有人，保持初心，不断前行。即使是失败，也是一次有意义的失败。做过总比不做强。我仍然期待看到各位成功的那天！不管是在哪个赛道、哪个行业、哪个领域，都祝大家未来心想事成。:LIS_pixel_heart:

[h1] 《恶校游戏》简评 [/h1]
《恶校游戏》讲述了有关校园欺凌与复仇这两个要素的策略影视作品，游戏中不管是演员的表演还是游戏的玩法都让人非常的有代入感，玩起来特别的沉浸。

剧情一开始游戏就叙述了一起校园欺凌，游戏中玩家将扮演被欺负的顾盼雨的妹妹顾盼晴，因一次旧物的清理揭开了姐姐被霸凌多年的真相，随着剧情的深入，玩家会发现，事情远远比人所想像的要更加冷血。

在游戏中，为了避免纯粹的剧情推进枯燥，游戏中还有一些简单的互动，例如滑动，点击或者是限时点击，让玩家在推进剧情的时候也能有自身的参与感。游戏里的情报收集是具有特色的一点，有点影视作品里那味儿了，收集情报，整理，定下策略，游戏的谋划这点做的还是可以的，就如同在钢丝上行走一样，一步出错就会导致游戏的结局变化，非常的细节。

单章节的复仇计划还是特别的爽快的，游戏内的场景设计的非常真实，细致的设计让玩家在推进游戏进度的时候仿佛自身就在其中一样，从发现目标，收集情报，制定计划，实施方案，这每一步都有着具体的描绘与叙述，玩家将带入复仇者的视角，参与到这一系列的剧情中。

总的来说，《恶校游戏》是一款制作精良，演员演技出色，玩法丰富的校园欺凌类互动影视作品，游戏中玩家将以一位复仇者的视角参与到游戏的互动中，游戏中的场景设计的非常不错，互动的玩法也很简单，那种一步步复仇的感觉特别
爽快，让人不由自主的就沉浸在了游戏的剧情中。

神人一般的抽象剧情，让人不忍思考编剧的文化水平，就是女主一路爽杀，既无游戏性也无观赏性，还有我们经典的[spoiler]按着玩家的头宽恕霸凌者的[/spoiler]神秘剧情。而且到头来并不是跟所谓霸凌有关，无非是个爽文复仇小故事罢了。

一部让人哭笑不得的闹剧，剧本为了悬疑而悬疑，剧情为了砂仁而砂仁，题材为了霸凌而霸凌，悬疑影游的每一个要素都占了，但是每一项都如空中楼阁一般，剧本建立在一个空气做的地基上，这是一部和现实完全脱节的，反映霸凌现象的非现实题材互动影游。
值得肯定的是，这部互动影游有一定自知之明，中不中日不日的洋泾浜行为，可以用来解释这是日本的华侨学校，进而将这部剧诸多不可能发生的事件，归结于这里既不算传统意义上的日本，也不是大陆，可以规避一些较为麻烦的审查和解释一下浅显的逻辑漏洞。但是作为一个在人类社会发生的事件，还是不能规避这部剧过于离谱的设定和剧情。董事长李启铭，作为校董，一位有权有势的BOSS，为什么在有一堆目击者的情况下主动把自己的软肋端到这些人眼前，在不是自己第一个致女主姐姐受伤的情况下，在女儿还没有铸成杀人大错的情况下，强行捅了女主姐姐一刀（如果不捅，这部互动电影不成立）但是作为一个有权有势的人，这种人会这么轻易的授人以柄，实在让人百思不得其解。而且剧情中期铺垫李启铭有权有势，阴险狡猾，结局轻易就被女主设计绑架，完成了复仇，也足够敷衍。
剧情中李启铭的反常只能理解为作为校董的他患有精神分裂，所以在对自己有百害而无一利的情况下，给女主姐姐来了这么一刀，然后看了结尾的我们知道，有收藏癖的李启铭最后把女主姐姐的尸骨转移到自己宅基地，方便以后东窗事发，警察能在第一时间联想到谁是凶手。
看这部互动影游不能过脑子，一旦过了脑子就会发现导演和编剧把所有观众都当成了智障。但是这部影游又搞了这些悬疑感，有那么一点杀人魔王金田一，一集屠一群人的感觉，只不过，看少年金田一，观众看完一集，了解到真相会有复仇的爽感，看这部互动影游，观众看完完全没有什么复仇的爽感，因为开挂了的，人见人爱的女主，杀的的要么是精神病要么是低智人。
初次了解这款游戏是在小黑盒，所谓的解散公告里，得知这部游戏刚发售就要解散，而且制作人不吝溢美之词，在介绍这款游戏时用了瑕不掩瑜，T1级别，问心无愧等话语，那篇公告当即就引起了我的好奇和惋惜。直到这部影游的片尾字幕结束后，我终于从眼前一黑，如坐针毡，变成了啼笑皆非，无可奈何的大彻大悟之中，我终于明白《牛来》这样一部神片为什么能赢得市场，毕竟怎么样都是输，我上我也行，至少能让观众自己为自己加冕，而不是陷入素不相识的人的自我感动。

[h1]《恶校游戏》|  个人评分：84/100 [/h1]
一款真人影视互动类游戏，没有擦边，没有恋爱，非常纯粹的女主复仇情节，没放过任何一个坏人，并且还赢得了好结局，过程相当爽快。
游戏前期塑造的情节沉浸感挺足的，并且流程相当流畅，没有什么比较出戏的环节，真的是看出制作组有在打磨，但是越到后面感觉剧情有点赶，尤其是最后一章，正义感爆棚的JC刚在前一章出场，最后一章剧情戏份又没给多少，就到直接反派瞬间降智完成草草结束。
整个游戏流程不是很长，大概三个小时左右就能探索全部，剧情也算比较严谨的阵列，有点可惜的是没控制好成本，制作组被解散。

还算不错，人物刻画很丰满，剧情也很有戏剧性。和前面章节的两种选择对比，结尾显得有些草草赶工，而且事件本身些许缺乏真实性。但瑕不掩瑜，能把校园暴力拍的如此淋漓尽致，能刻画出每个人在这个漩涡中的挣扎与沉沦，已经算是相当优秀的作品。
只要社会不改变，教育不改变，立法执法司法不改变，校园暴力永远不会消失。它不是某个人的一时作恶，它是整个环境共同孕育出的的恶果。

拉完了，我想问一下剧本是人写出来的吗？剧情乱七八糟，强行煽情强行90度转折，比如上一秒两个女主被鬼怪禁锢，下一秒就在出现在家里的沙发上和男主打情骂俏。这类莫名其妙的衔接充斥在整个游戏里面，虽然恋游玩家对剧本包容度很高，但你也不能写的像山与海那个逼制作组一样吧。还有那个古铜色皮肤的女主，丑的要死戏份还给那么多，反而楼泠像个客串的。唯一有正向反馈的地方就是马与鹿吵架那一段。顺道夸一下马倩倩演技还是一如既往的稳，由于浩浩妈瘦了很多，观感没有以前的作品好了。

这类型游戏，就三个方面，要么游戏性，要么剧情性，要么福利性。
目前在这个游戏上什么都看不出来哪里有什么好的。
游戏性：
1. 经典防退款QTE玩法，这个画符的玩法是谁研究的，搞出来这个东西干嘛。
2. 加入了欲念值，到现在我也没研究出来这个东西新加入的意义。有的选择界面也没提示出这个欲念到底加没加。（在此说一句，发教程的大佬还标出来数值的是真牛逼啊）

剧情：那就更别说了，一大堆人出现的莫名其妙，感情线莫名其妙，男主就这么魅魔啊，鬼王剧情少的要命，到现在就拿了老马和鬼王小姐姐的全成就，玩不下去了，又臭又长，顶不住了。
 
福利：不是查边露个沟就是福利啊，搞什么集贸啊，
也玩了那么多这类型的游戏了，怎么着怎么烂我也会全成就，不然有蚂蚁在爬，直到出现了这个游戏。看着阵容强大。头一回玩这游戏玩两个角色就边刷短视频边玩游戏了。没意思

本来这神人游戏制作方场外风波就很多了，但这和我这种只玩游戏的没干系，我又懒得弄什么签名，但是这游戏实在太弱智了，什么傻逼剧情和低能儿男主，男主智商加上爱因斯坦的智商再翻个倍碰上范小勤都是生死局，前脚知道有人给他们下药找上门去算账，后脚人家当着他面下的毒这脑瘫男主还喝下去了，剧情还不连贯，一跳一跳的，刷短视频都没这么跳跃过，男主还是个废物，出门碰到个蚂蚁都要点投降的那种，很难说是类人生物，人类进化居然最后有男主这么个产物，小行星当年还是直接把地球毁灭了吧，论剧情没脑子，论男主是废物，找个女主还是替代品，弄个山寨货，装造表演痕迹全往王涵身上靠，给陈漫设计这么个八婆角色，你们的编剧是师从豆包吗，感觉不如直接让豆包来。
好尴尬的演技，水剧情，为了消遣来玩的，人工呼吸你按锁骨啊，有没有一点文化啊
纯纯的垃圾影游，虽然由于演员本身演技水平过关整体可以勉强游玩下去，但是除了肖倩有一些基本的人物塑造外，其他的角色压根没有塑造，显得十分生硬，最过分的是，游戏本身的5毛钱特效让人看了十分不舒服，还有那离谱降智的神人剧情，是纯纯地老鼠屎，我本来以为完蛋的盛夏离开与合本身已经靠着足够的炒冷饭与弱智剧情刷新了国内影游的下限，没想到，还有高手
剧情真的太烂了，人物完全没有铺垫，逻辑混乱，也就是靠演员撑着了，玩了三个小时真是折磨，要不是为了看马倩倩都没有玩下去的欲望了。

终于有网了，前段时间完美通关了，但是离线游玩没办法评论。
以下是缺点：
1.官方签名照活动整体非常垃圾。真的伤了不少玩家(不过这是不是也说明了有不少影游都是靠签名照刷的好评呐？我不知道，不好讲，怕被告。幸好我不要签名照)
2.整体剧情非常无聊，也就马倩倩老师演的倩女幽魂的故事整体世界线比较完整，但还是整体故事发展比较生硬。其他角色更不用说了。玩完不知道讲的什么。
而且非要加一个黑妹，荒岛求生也是加了个黑妹，也没卖多好。制作组懂审美吗？
3.悬疑伏笔回收潦草，最终反派退场仓促。什么鬼啊？而且一些道具藏的非常深。制作组就纯属有病
4.可能涉及到收买一些测评博主，你有那个钱，研究研究剧本不行？增加点拍摄预算(有的地方能看出明显ai感)
5.修罗场占比过高：多角冲突戏份挤压单人感情线，单人线塑造偏薄，不喜欢修罗场的玩家反感。
6.浩浩妈的故事更是一坨(最后结局竟然能看见“奶盖”？)
7.节奏割裂：校园喜剧→灵异惊悚→修罗场恋爱频繁硬切，缺少过渡，让人出戏。
8.完美结局需同时控好感+欲念值(更关键的是欲念值一周目还不给你，用屁眼想的？)
剧情不知所谓，没有任何前因后果，全靠老师颜值硬撑，但几个老师的角色也没有任何新鲜感可言，王新晨妆造很奇怪，脖子太长，陈老师老演这种角色，非常腻，马倩倩的角色跟表演也很拉，跟之前那个小师妹没有任何区别。。。总之除非是粉丝，否则完全不推荐

[h1]梅衣阁诗人[/h1]
“影游”这个概念已经诞生很久了，尚不清楚这类游戏在国外的表现如何，但至少在国内，在2023年《完蛋》系列出现之前，一直处于不温不火的状态，但现如今，无论是效仿《完蛋》的恋爱题材，还是纯粹的真人互动影视剧，几乎都在同一时间涌现出大量作品，其中不乏各种各样的佳作。

《完蛋》早期的模仿者们大都不被看好，不少玩家都认为这只不过会是一时的风靡罢了，不会持续很久......但事实证明，“美少女恋爱向影游”的市场依旧是一片欣欣向荣，或源于现实中糟糕的恋爱体验，或又是单纯不喜欢与二次元纸片人谈恋爱，或仅仅就是享受这种真人交互的体验，越来越多的玩家把目光开始投向这些作品。

而在“后《完蛋》”时代，吃过细糠的观众/玩家们，对于“美少女恋爱”题材的作品愈发挑剔，制作组们只能不断的卷剧情卷制作，以此期待获得玩家的青睐——这样“百家争鸣”的局面无疑是极端利好玩家的，越来越多的优质作品竞相登场——例如本作。

说实话，就影片水平而言，本作在我心目中绝对是排不上号的，有一说一，我感觉女角色说话的声音糊糊的，听起来很难受，此外特效也有些过于廉价了。

但我为什么还是给到推荐？因为本作做到了许多同类型产品想都不敢想的东西：游戏性。

本作存在大量QTE小游戏，这在很大程度上丰富了玩家的体验，我终于在影游中体验到了“反应过慢导致的失败”。

结合游戏整体素质，我强烈推荐各位购入本作，体验一下真正的影“游”。
[quote]
我的游戏真的有那么好玩吗?
关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/34823631/]“我的游戏不可能那么好玩！”鉴赏家[/url],这是你从未体验过的船新版本~
[/quote]
可以说美女系列的后作 虽然不是美女系列的原厂 但是气息浓厚 不管怎样 非常看好这种类型的影游 这才是影游应该要有的 未来可期

校园悬疑风真人互动影游。

男主因意外释放千年女鬼，获得了能看清“里世界”阴阳眼的特殊能力，然后跟六位女主产生交集，逐渐调查出隐藏在其现实背后的真相。虽然游戏里真的有鬼，但是鬼妆造不吓人，也不会有那种跳吓，胆小的玩家完全不用担心。

本作最大卖点是演员阵容强大，六位妹子个个都是影游里的热门人物，有陈漫、王星辰、鹿蓝予、楼泠、马倩倩跟米妮。画面拍摄清晰，给的福利镜头数量也不少，加之角色颜值本来就高，所以观感还是不错的。

游戏可玩性不错，每位角色都有普通、好跟完美三个结局可解锁（还有随着拼图碎片拼好后解锁的专属小视频），其中完美结局需要同时满足角色欲念跟好感值，好在二周目会给予欲念显示提示，攻略起来并不难就是了。

该作曾叫《鬼才和你谈恋爱》，由于某些原因下架了，后面虽然重新改名上架了，但是剧本也进行了阉割删减，导致不少地方衔接生硬，看得有点跳戏。所以对于在意剧情逻辑的玩家来说，这款游戏带给你的体验可能就不是很好了。
[quote]
加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ADZZW]爱の榨汁屋[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/34815366/]爱の鉴赏家[/url]，用爱品鉴世间作品，用心流淌真情实感。
[/quote]

一开始我就是奔着浩浩妈和欧阳老师来的，结果玩到最后完全选择不了，每一个演员不仅都顶级颜值身材还福利满满,这叫我咋选！！玩到最后反而我最喜欢殷柠，如果制作组能再把她邀请过来拍一部的话我将感激不尽。
  玩法方面确实很多样化，比我之前玩的互动游戏体量都要大，确实是做出了一些玩法上的突破，还加入了像召唤术变选项等有创意的点。
  至于剧情方面我实在是无力吐槽，不知道是不是删减的原因，太神头鬼脑了我完全无法参透，只能说要在复杂的玩法基础上做剧情还是太为难了。总体来说不赖，这个打折价格买了就一玩一个不吱声了。
纯纯的垃圾影游，虽然由于演员本身演技水平过关整体可以勉强游玩下去，但是除了肖倩有一些基本的人物塑造外，其他的角色压根没有塑造，显得十分生硬，最过分的是，游戏本身的5毛钱特效让人看了十分不舒服，还有那离谱降智的神人剧情，是纯纯地老鼠屎，我本来以为完蛋的盛夏离开与合本身已经靠着足够的炒冷饭与弱智剧情刷新了国内影游的下限，没想到，还有高手
剧情真的太烂了，人物完全没有铺垫，逻辑混乱，也就是靠演员撑着了，玩了三个小时真是折磨，要不是为了看马倩倩都没有玩下去的欲望了。
好大的。。。。。。游戏。制作组真的懂怎么擦。。。。。亮玩家的眼睛，越玩越好玩。其实已经玩了第三章，见到了浩浩妈，但是觉得不完美，重新来过了。推荐，推荐。
剧情不知所谓，没有任何前因后果，全靠老师颜值硬撑，但几个老师的角色也没有任何新鲜感可言，王新晨妆造很奇怪，脖子太长，陈老师老演这种角色，非常腻，马倩倩的角色跟表演也很拉，跟之前那个小师妹没有任何区别。。。总之除非是粉丝，否则完全不推荐

终于有网了，前段时间完美通关了，但是离线游玩没办法评论。
以下是缺点：
1.官方签名照活动整体非常垃圾。真的伤了不少玩家(不过这是不是也说明了有不少影游都是靠签名照刷的好评呐？我不知道，不好讲，怕被告。幸好我不要签名照)
2.整体剧情非常无聊，也就马倩倩老师演的倩女幽魂的故事整体世界线比较完整，但还是整体故事发展比较生硬。其他角色更不用说了。玩完不知道讲的什么。
而且非要加一个黑妹，荒岛求生也是加了个黑妹，也没卖多好。制作组懂审美吗？
3.悬疑伏笔回收潦草，最终反派退场仓促。什么鬼啊？而且一些道具藏的非常深。制作组就纯属有病
4.可能涉及到收买一些测评博主，你有那个钱，研究研究剧本不行？增加点拍摄预算(有的地方能看出明显ai感)
5.修罗场占比过高：多角冲突戏份挤压单人感情线，单人线塑造偏薄，不喜欢修罗场的玩家反感。
6.浩浩妈的故事更是一坨(最后结局竟然能看见“奶盖”？)
7.节奏割裂：校园喜剧→灵异惊悚→修罗场恋爱频繁硬切，缺少过渡，让人出戏。
8.完美结局需同时控好感+欲念值(更关键的是欲念值一周目还不给你，用屁眼想的？)
剧情方面一般吧，演员这一块很好很顶级马倩倩很夯，ui不错，期待下一部作品

我叫蔡晨，一次偶然的机会我获得了与众不同的能力，我的阴阳眼可以看到别人看不到的东西，这到底是福是祸我也不知道。

《不心动才有鬼》这是一款悬疑解密的互动影游。男主是一名大学生，剧情上有很多校园日常，玩的时候很有学习的味道。

“化玄机”是游戏的重要玩法之一，不仅可以操控自然界的元素，还可以窥视人心，读懂各位女主内心所想，想想就很刺激。法术需在支线中解锁，如果在对话中使用对应的法术，就可以解锁不一样的剧情。除了“化玄机”外，还有QTE、画符、罗盘等玩法。

结局的反转让我很意外，“蔡晨蔡晨”我是“采臣”，原来这都是前世种下的因果，这一切都是鬼王惹的麻烦。游戏中有大量电影对应的情节，有种既熟悉又陌生的感觉。在玩家通关后会解锁欲念值，好感度和欲念值要达到一定数值后才会解锁每一位女主的完美结局，这种双线的判定一定程度上会使剧情解锁变繁琐，但也增加了游戏玩法的丰富性，有利也有弊吧。

这部作品的优点也是可圈可点，先说演员阵容吧，有不少大家熟知的面孔，角色选择贴合人设，演技就更不用说了。游戏的配乐也很有特色，在剧情高潮时不会显得突兀，在剧情平淡时可以起到很好的过渡作用。

《不心动才有鬼》总得来说是一款不错的影游，虽然在场外有一些节奏，但也不影响它是个好游戏。

Steam好评：诚意满满的唐风宫廷互动影游，氛围感拉满
入手《女王的游戏：盛世天下媚娘篇》放了很久没碰，最近想找一款不肝不氪、适合休闲放松的单机游戏，终于翻出来体验了一番。原本只是随手一试，没想到直接被惊艳到，作为一款真人互动影游，它的整体质感远超我的预期，也是我近期玩过最有沉浸感的宫廷题材互动作品，特此认真写个中肯评价。
首先必须重点夸爆游戏的影视级制作水准。上线数月热度依旧能打不是没有道理的，整体深宫氛围感直接拉满，完全是正规古装电视剧的质感。服化道称得上是同类互动游戏里的一流水准，高度贴合唐代宫廷风格，布景精致考究、细节满满，画面构图、镜头运镜都对标院线剧集和网剧水准，观影体验极其舒服。唯一小小的瑕疵就是部分角色妆容偏浓艳，稍微有点违和，除此之外所有场景、造型、画面呈现都恰到好处，观感挑不出大毛病。
再说演员演绎与剧情表现，整体属于稳中有亮点的水平。没有顶尖影视剧的精湛演技，但绝非粗制滥造的流水线短剧质感，甚至吊打市面上大部分低成本网剧，演员表情自然、代入感足。剧情方面偶尔会有小幅跳脱、节奏衔接不够流畅的问题，但瑕不掩瑜，多条人物线的刻画细腻又戳人，有好几处情节让我全程动容，后劲很足。
最打动我的有三处剧情设计，搭配配乐直接封神。第一是李承乾的知己情与爱而不得，这段剧情没有刻意煽情，却把隐忍、遗憾、求而不得的无奈刻画得淋漓尽致，适配的主题曲和歌词完美贴合心境，氛围感直接拉满，大幅提升剧情感染力。第二是公主与小和尚的虐心羁绊，初心动的纯粹美好，对上帝王身不由己的宿命、小和尚舍己成全的隐忍克制，出身皇家的身不由己、爱而不得的遗憾被诠释得淋漓尽致，后续剧情铺垫和配乐加持，让这段BE美学格外戳心。第三是韦贵妃的结局线，她的落幕不是单纯的反派落幕，而是满含母亲的柔软与牵挂，对女儿的执念与不舍，一步步造就了自己的没落，人物立体饱满，演技和剧情双重加持，让人彻底共情，格外触动人心。
玩过不少同类互动影游，包括热门的完蛋系列，一直以来我都不太擅长分支选择类玩法，总觉得多数作品只是单纯靠选项推进剧情，缺乏深度。但这款游戏彻底打破了我的固有印象，它不只是简单的“选选项、走剧情”，每一次选择都需要深思熟虑，贴合宫廷权谋的生存逻辑，兼顾了娱乐性和思考性。玩家的每一个抉择都关乎走向，没有无脑通关的套路，沉浸式体验拉满，真正做到了让人代入武媚娘步步为营的宫廷人生。
整体而言，这是一款诚意十足、质感上乘的宫廷互动影游。影视级的视听体验、立体饱满的人物塑造、细腻走心的剧情台词，还有恰到好处的配乐加持，足以碾压多数同类作品。虽然存在剧情小幅跳跃、妆容略显浮夸、演技不算顶级的小瑕疵，但完全不影响整体游玩体验。
适合喜欢古风宫廷、权谋剧情、沉浸式观影体验的玩家入手，休闲游玩、慢慢代入剧情格外合适，绝对是同类互动游戏里的优质佳作，值得入手体验。

入手《女王的游戏：盛世天下媚娘篇》放了很久没碰，最近想找一款不肝不氪、适合休闲放松的单机游戏，终于翻出来体验了一番。原本只是随手一试，没想到直接被惊艳到，作为一款真人互动影游，它的整体质感远超我的预期，也是我近期玩过最有沉浸感的宫廷题材互动作品，特此认真写个中肯评价。
首先必须重点夸爆游戏的影视级制作水准。上线数月热度依旧能打不是没有道理的，整体深宫氛围感直接拉满，完全是正规古装电视剧的质感。服化道称得上是同类互动游戏里的一流水准，高度贴合唐代宫廷风格，布景精致考究、细节满满，画面构图、镜头运镜都对标院线剧集和网剧水准，观影体验极其舒服。唯一小小的瑕疵就是部分角色妆容偏浓艳，稍微有点违和，除此之外所有场景、造型、画面呈现都恰到好处，观感挑不出大毛病。
再说演员演绎与剧情表现，整体属于稳中有亮点的水平。没有顶尖影视剧的精湛演技，但绝非粗制滥造的流水线短剧质感，甚至吊打市面上大部分低成本网剧，演员表情自然、代入感足。剧情方面偶尔会有小幅跳脱、节奏衔接不够流畅的问题，但瑕不掩瑜，多条人物线的刻画细腻又戳人，有好几处情节让我全程动容，后劲很足。
最打动我的有三处剧情设计，搭配配乐直接封神。第一是李承乾的知己情与爱而不得，这段剧情没有刻意煽情，却把隐忍、遗憾、求而不得的无奈刻画得淋漓尽致，适配的主题曲和歌词完美贴合心境，氛围感直接拉满，大幅提升剧情感染力。第二是公主与小和尚的虐心羁绊，初心动的纯粹美好，对上帝王身不由己的宿命、小和尚舍己成全的隐忍克制，出身皇家的身不由己、爱而不得的遗憾被诠释得淋漓尽致，后续剧情铺垫和配乐加持，让这段BE美学格外戳心。第三是韦贵妃的结局线，她的落幕不是单纯的反派落幕，而是满含母亲的柔软与牵挂，对女儿的执念与不舍，一步步造就了自己的没落，人物立体饱满，演技和剧情双重加持，让人彻底共情，格外触动人心。
玩过不少同类互动影游，包括热门的完蛋系列，一直以来我都不太擅长分支选择类玩法，总觉得多数作品只是单纯靠选项推进剧情，缺乏深度。但这款游戏彻底打破了我的固有印象，它不只是简单的“选选项、走剧情”，每一次选择都需要深思熟虑，贴合宫廷权谋的生存逻辑，兼顾了娱乐性和思考性。玩家的每一个抉择都关乎走向，没有无脑通关的套路，沉浸式体验拉满，真正做到了让人代入武媚娘步步为营的宫廷人生。
整体而言，这是一款诚意十足、质感上乘的宫廷互动影游。影视级的视听体验、立体饱满的人物塑造、细腻走心的剧情台词，还有恰到好处的配乐加持，足以碾压多数同类作品。虽然存在剧情小幅跳跃、妆容略显浮夸、演技不算顶级的小瑕疵，但完全不影响整体游玩体验。
适合喜欢古风宫廷、权谋剧情、沉浸式观影体验的玩家入手，休闲游玩、慢慢代入剧情格外合适，绝对是同类互动游戏里的优质佳作，值得入手体验。

This is a very unique game that there is no “easy” mode for.  If you enjoy forensic detective work, you’re gonna love this game.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HKl3YSj9Tao&feature=youtu.be

This is a truly unique game where puzzles are not right in front of you, waiting to be solved.  There is some digging required.  There is no office assistant that will point you in the right direction.  You need to find clues, figure out what to do with them, and uncover more evidence.  Every door you open leads to a new door or maybe a window that is locked.  But there is no straightforward linear path to get out of said room.  

I loved the unique and hard gameplay, but that may turn off some gamers that want an easy ride.  If you enjoy a challenge, a deep game, and a weird story, give it a shot.

Note:  this is an adult game.  Adult language and themes throughout.  If off putting language is not your thing, don’t explore the Deepweb!

P.S.  great music!

i was totally unfamiliar with project deepweb, but found this game when scrolling through new psychological horror games. i thought i'd get a fun, maybe 2-4 hour "explore the creepy deepweb" game. 

boy, was i wrong. i'm 17 hours in and i feel like i'm at the tip of the iceberg.

i am completely blown away by the quality and quantity of gameplay and materials in this game. it feels totally smooth to play, and isn't JUST a click-around-on-the-desktop game. there is voice acting, live action recordings (including a phenomenal, disturbing, dark web-themed live action "livestream" you get to watch), real life code breaking, a fascinating hidden story, and even some random "minigames", for lack of a better word.

there are dozens of hidden secrets and content. to this moment, there is unsolved content in the game that the community is trying to solve. you get different interactions with different characters based on at what part of the game you talk to them. these interactions lead to more mysteries and more uncertainties. 

playing this game feels like solving an ARG that was made for you specifically. you truly feel as if you are in the protagonist's shoes and are going crazy yourself as you try to wrap up all the loose ends and get lost in a seemingly never-ending online world. you never stop asking yourself, "is this it? the final link, the final mystery solved?" the answer, always, is "no." 

if you like deep dive games that involve light scares, unnerving storylines, endless information you can choose to ignore or absorb, unraveling a mystery, and extracting valuable puzzle pieces from text, this game is for you. this game is like if welcome to the game 2 was good and you didn't have to deal with the IRL stuff.

speaking of IRL, this game ties into your real life -- you, sitting at the computer, not the protagonist you're playing as -- in eerie and unexpected ways. i still get shivers thinking about some of the IRL aspects included. 

if you're clever and brave enough, it may even enter your IRL life in ways you would never, ever expect from a video game. 

please play, and please join me and others in going insane over the endless mysteries. we could use the help!

This is a truly unique game where puzzles are not right in front of you, waiting to be solved.  There is some digging required.  There is no office assistant that will point you in the right direction.  You need to find clues, figure out what to do with them, and uncover more evidence.  Every door you open leads to a new door or maybe a window that is locked.  But there is no straightforward linear path to get out of said room.  

I loved the unique and hard gameplay, but that may turn off some gamers that want an easy ride.  If you enjoy a challenge, a deep game, and a weird story, give it a shot.

Note:  this is an adult game.  Adult language and themes throughout.  If off putting language is not your thing, don’t explore the Deepweb!

P.S.  great music!

[h1]光与影之恋[/h1]

[h2]游戏内容[/h2]

在卡特里兰“深造”的女主楚鹤白得知爷爷去世的消息后，就踏上回家之路，因为太多年没回来了，面对这座熟悉又陌生的城市，思绪连篇，看着正在崩溃的世界，车窗外剩下半截的墙体以及瓦砾中褪色的招牌《招牌牛肉汤面》，想起了这是自己走的时候，在这里吃的最后一顿。而点灯人总是把楚鹤白不愿意面对的事情说出来，点灯人是只有楚鹤白才可以看到的幽灵。在车里，从报纸上，吴姐、点灯人的嘴里得知，爷爷死的很突然，现在由姐姐楚鹤羽担任集团新掌门人，并且运营集团方式很是激进，让一些集团本地派对她这种方式很不满意，面对点灯人的提问：你真没考虑过在报纸上的可能是你吗？这句话让楚鹤白深思起来，但是楚鹤白也明白，自己接手，只会把所有的事情搞砸。到达目的地后，满满的记者和相机、闪光灯在等着楚鹤白，也议论纷纷，这时候楚鹤羽姐姐出马，杀鸡儆猴的处理了一位非议之人，并且堵住了现场其他议论声音，再来找到妹妹楚鹤白，让她追悼会结束后来自己车里一下，为啥来车里呢，当时因为是车上有很多小熊饼干啊。故事就此展开。

[h2]个人游玩体验分享[/h2]

百合大法好，游戏中百合这块内容做的还是很不多的，但是没有H内容不要想多了，游戏的剧情部分个人觉得写的挺不错的，人物塑造的也可以，并且还有多结局。游戏的画风好看，人物立绘，以及萌版人物都做的很可爱，并且很形象，看着不由得微微一笑，并且音乐也搭，玩起来给人的体验很不错。还有就是这游戏有配音，历史对话也有语音重播，并且历史对话还有跳转功能，这点虽然不稀奇吧，但是有这个功能真的省事很多，点赞。

[h2]结语[/h2]
《光与影之恋 Chiaroscuro Lovers》这款百合题材的视觉小说，画面制作出色，人物立绘以及萌版都做的很可爱，剧情质量扎实，感兴趣的话可以尝试一下。

欢迎关注：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/46039267/] 睡不醒的早八人 [/url] [/quote]

百合向短篇视觉小说。

故事以名为“大崩塌”的全球性地质灾害作为背景，地壳持续动荡重塑世界格局。楚氏集团依靠极端环境防护、生物医疗技术在灾难中崛起，却也深陷内部权斗与外部觊觎。玩家将扮演楚氏二小姐楚鹤白，十一年前因创伤失忆旅居海外，在心因性失明、时常伴随幻听幻视的状态下生活。爷爷离世的消息迫使她返乡，直面复杂的家族纠葛，和被长久封存的过往真相。

本作并非甜腻的日常恋爱，着重探讨“是否要铭记伤痛”跟“放下与告别”两种人生选择，整体基调偏伤感，是带有悲剧底色的情感向故事。游戏里主要登场的角色有四位，分别是主角楚鹤白、楚鹤羽、于琳跟长得很像于琳的点灯人，其中楚鹤白跟楚鹤羽的立绘，于琳跟点灯人的立绘各自都很像，前面一对因为是姐妹的关系，至于后面一对，虽然作为伏笔会在游戏最后部分揭示答案，但是聪明的你估计看一下就能猜到吧。

游戏带有多选项多结局设定，全程国语配音（主人公也有配音，质量好，很自然）。整体演出挺不错的，在正常叙事路线中插入大量回忆片段（回忆时画面右上角会标注“回忆”两字，很贴心，生怕玩家搞混，所以该作剧情理解起来也十分的顺畅），然后根据几个选项导向不同的结局。有意思的是游戏中段跟每个结局都单独做了专属音乐MV，给人看得一下子高大上了起来。而且这些音乐及其歌词跟当前路线和做出选择导向的结局也是紧密联系的，更能放大情绪感染力，加深玩家对剧情的共情与记忆。

顺带一提，游戏通关后并未真正结束，开启二周目后会新增选项，选择后虽然剧情脉络没怎么变，但会为增加更多的故事细节。

这是一部约4小时流程的国产百合短篇，成就基本为流程杯或结局杯，全成就比较友好。开头部分确实有些谜语人，“精卫计划”“红海计划”“本土派”“海外派”等名词轮番出现，一度让人以为作者只是在堆设定、掉书袋。好在后续展开紧扣“精卫计划”，随着记忆一点点找回，主角逐步面对过去不敢触碰的真相，并最终与过去和解，观感回升明显。

[h2]角色塑造[/h2]
三位女主形象区分度不错：楚鹤羽表面霸总、实则娇妻；于琳性格内敛，偏阴沉系；还有一直陪在身边的“点灯人”。

不过她们爱着的，多少都是“过去的我”。过去的我简直是圣母式角色：在楚鹤羽受人挑拨、想杀她夺取继承人位置换取自由时，选择原谅并毅然赴死；在于琳深陷阴影无法自拔时，一遍遍劝慰她，带她逃离，带她看星星。

因此这一世带着零记忆归来后，会有一种“我明明什么都没做，却处处留情”的错位感。前期的大量发糖，因后续部分感情线尚未展开叙述，而略缺铺垫，观感有些生硬。

然我即是我，不是来自过去的幽灵。女主失忆后，虽说与过去不同，多了些毒舌。但善良，为他人着想的特质依旧没变。所以前期女主们对我的感情，是一种带着愧疚的，对过去的投影。而后面更像是重新认识，重新爱上我，并将过去与现在重叠起来

[h2]叙事与演出[/h2]
中后期以寻找记忆为主线，回忆与现实频繁交替，整体稍显凌乱，但基本还能分得清。情感表达的关键段落会采用主题曲演出，全篇大约有六七处，能看出投入不小，氛围感也撑起来了。

如果说我是别人的小太阳，那点灯人（于欣），即是我的小太阳。在温暖别人的同时，我自己也是个病弱的可怜少女，而她莽莽撞撞地闯进我的生活，用热情感染着我。大崩塌中，她献出了自己的心脏，此后便以点灯人的身份，活在我的意识里。当我终于发现真相，她也只是温柔地原谅了我。也许意识里的她只是一个幻影，但她陪我走过了无数孤独与脆弱的时刻。如果她还在世，也一定会这样选择。

整体刀子偏多，每个人都有自己的痛苦和无奈。但女主似乎就如小太阳一般，敢想敢做，照开她人的阴霾。不过后续专注于故事展开，还是想多看到与现在两位的糖啊

琉璃花糖制作组的新百合作品来啦！这次的游戏初期悬疑感拉满，玩家扮演一个失忆的拄拐的有心理创伤的少女楚鹤白，拥有一个不错的身世，但是却面对各种困难。游戏初期给我的感觉像是一个被四处打击的主角突破自我的故事，但是实际上游戏整体却是一个充满爱与甜的故事。

游戏的剧情主要讲述的是一个关于记忆、创伤和爱的短篇故事，通过主要的两个分支选项来达成不同的三个结局。在游戏的过程中玩家逐渐解开心中的疑惑，寻找到爱的源头。游戏的文本相当优秀，甜甜的甚至有一点好哭。尤其是点灯人的那句“放手吧，点灯人累了”真的有一种泪崩的感觉。

游戏画风是一种特别的手绘风格，很有鲜明的特色，立绘看上去偏日常感，主角的一些表情看起来非常可爱。游戏的过程中还有一些Q版角色画面，Q版人物更可爱，也为当时的剧情故事做了氛围铺垫。游戏的BGM也是一种轻柔的轻松的氛围。登场角色基本上都有配音，质量还是非常不错的，配音老师辛苦了。

唯一的遗憾大概就是游戏的篇幅过于短了，总有一种意犹未尽的感觉，而且我也期待更加明显更加多样的百合内容，游戏这方面呈现出来的数量有点少了。

总的来说，作为白河豚这款游戏我还是非常推荐入手的，琉璃花糖制作组的百合糖值得信赖。尤其是本作的主人公还是一个我很喜欢的性格的魅魔，很有代入感。这个世界也是温柔的，有爱的，善良的。

[h1]于光影中，寻找过去的自我[/h1]

[h2]游戏简介[/h2]
《光与影之恋Chiaroscuro Lovers》是一款由琉璃花糖制作组倾心打造的百合治愈gal——一个关于记忆、创伤以及爱的故事。游戏中我们将跟随楚鹤白的视角，当失忆十一年后的她因爷爷的葬礼重回故乡、故地重游。熟悉的街景、故人的面庞如潮水般向她涌来，那些刻意或无意遗忘的碎片，也在光影交错间悄然复苏。因此，一场关于寻找自我的故事开始了。

[h2]游戏内容[/h2]
故事发生在一个因剧烈地壳运动导致全球性灾难“大崩塌”的末日下，我们的主角楚鹤白所在的本家“楚氏集团”也在这场大崩塌下因掌握“极端环境防护技术”和“生物医疗”而收益颇丰。但是随着她的爷爷，楚氏集团掌权人的离世，公司出现了俩种不同派系的声音——本土派和海外派。海外派支持红海计划，本土派则支持精卫计划。

而作为楚氏继承人，楚鹤白拥有最大的权利去决定公司走向，但在决定之前，楚鹤白首先要面对的，是比公司未来走向更棘手的事——她自己，就像她所说的“人人都爱楚鹤白，唯独我不认识楚鹤白”。

红海计划与精卫计划，代表着两种截然不同的未来：是放弃这片伤痕累累的土地远走海外，还是以精卫填海般重启计划、留守故乡？而楚鹤白的选择，终究需要她自己去寻找——她到底在逃避什么?那个让她在十一年前彻底失忆的真相，或许才是故事最终的结局。

[h2]游戏体验[/h2]
故事围绕楚鹤白、姐姐楚鹤羽、主治医师于琳，以及只有她能看见的幽灵少女点灯人展开，在她们的日常对话中，制作组设计了大量关于楚鹤白心理活动的描写，同时还利用过去与现在来回切换的手法，将楚鹤白的过去一一展现在我们面前。

[h1] 在这个末世里她就是你的灯[/h1]

[h2] 背景[/h2]
游戏里的世界正在经历一场【大崩塌】，也就是一场由剧烈地质运动导致的横贯全球的地质灾害，而且正有持续增强的迹象，整个人类文明都危在旦夕。
而楚氏集团凭借着【极端环境防护技术】和【生物医疗】这两项看家本领借机崛起，成为一代财阀，靠着抵御灾害收获颇丰，却也因为怀有能够创造巨大财富的技术而饱受觊觎。

[h2] 剧情起因[/h2]
我们的主角——楚鹤白，如今22岁，正是这个楚氏集团的二小姐。
楚鹤白从小就去了国外居住，也失去了小时候的记忆，无忧无虑地开着一家花店。如今，从国内传来一道消息，楚氏集团掌门人，也就是楚家老爷子，去世了。

因为爷爷去世而回到阔别已久的故乡，何况自己还是失去了很多记忆的状态，楚鹤白对一切都那么茫然。
也正是在家里，楚鹤白终于见到了多年不见的姐姐，如今的楚氏集团掌舵人楚鹤羽，她对下属是那么雷厉风行，却对自己这个妹妹如此温柔，但似乎。。。好像还有什么原因？

一直以来，楚鹤白的旁边都能看到一个白色头发的少女，自称为【点灯人】，她似乎永远没有烦心的事，也经常会笑嘻嘻的出来和楚鹤白吐槽。
但是——只有楚鹤白能够看见她，因为她是一个幽灵。

楚鹤白身上的病也很多，还好楚氏集团有着顶尖的医疗条件，而我们也能够在楚氏集团医院遇到院长于琳——一位医学天才同时也是个工作狂，总是顶着一头乱糟糟的白发，但是也能对治疗提出恰当的建议。

[h2] 谜团[/h2]
人人都爱楚鹤白，唯独我自己不认识过去的自己。
楚鹤白遇到的每个人都对她是那么的温柔，那么的贴心，但楚鹤白对她们，对自己都一无所知。

其实，当我们选择回到故乡接受寻找自己失去记忆的时刻，命运的齿轮就开始悄然传动。
过去到底发生了什么？主角楚鹤白为什么会失去记忆？这个世界还有救吗？
这一切的答案都藏在游戏里。

有些灯光，会被点亮。但也有些黑暗也许不该被照亮。
有些记忆，会被找回。但也有些真相也许会带来伤害。
但当我们勇敢走出那一步之后，也许会发现，这个世界以及她们，似乎都比想象中更温柔一些。

最后值得一提的是，每个结局环节还会配上CV亲自唱的不同歌曲一首，给每个结局带来更加沉浸式的体验。

—— 光灭了，影还在。影散了，光已入心。

整体和制作组之前作品“与神相伴的末日”似乎是同一世界观的意思。“大崩塌”危及人类文明存续的末日科技世界，从小体弱多病、本该早就死去却特殊原因存活好转，但仍患有“心因性失眠”拄拐+失忆的少女“楚鹤白”，因为爷爷去世而不得已回到阔别多年的故乡。
面对着其他人知晓、唯独自己茫然无知的“过去”；面对着只有她能看见的元气幽灵少女“点灯人”、对她百般呵护的霸总“姐姐”、十分珍视关心她的“天才女医师”——周围三位温柔亲密对待她、却都十分阻止你回想起过去的美少女。整体便是围绕着少女们的互动对白、以及女主过去记忆的相关话题，不断叙事。
如果过去是痛苦的，那么你是否又有勇气想起呢？

本作虽然有多结局、围绕在女主身边的三位美少女角色，但并非个人线的那种恋爱三选一类型，而是主角面对过往所做出的抉择面对；整体也并非很侧重百合恋爱感的样子、而是更为凸显创伤、关心与羁绊的“爱”的风格。
随着回忆与现实的交错演绎、游戏的故事碎片慢慢拼凑，从而让玩家逐渐理解那些阻止与痛苦感情的源头、明白楚鹤白失忆的原因、点灯人的身份、十一年前究竟发生了什么的真相。可能游戏的刀子倒也不算难猜，毕竟“只有我能看到的幽灵少女”这般人设，其实作为一把刀子而言藏得已经足够清晰了。
整体情绪铺垫得当，全程中文配音，画风尚可，喜欢带点忧郁刀子感百合作的玩家可以尝试一下。

《绍宋：还我河山》——此座可惜
在聊这款游戏之前，我想聊个历史典故，西晋开国皇帝司马炎的太子司马衷有智力障碍，当时的大臣看在眼里急在心里，尚书令卫瓘有一次喝多了就抚摸着皇位感慨“此座可惜”，司马炎也看在眼里，最后敷衍了一句说卫瓘喝多了，等到司马炎死后，司马衷登基之后，西晋的国祚也就没几天了。
为什么要聊这个呢，因为对于这款游戏和这段历史，我的评价就是“此座可惜”——用最好的IP做出来的中庸之作。
首先要承认，这款游戏真的没有魔改太多，但这游戏倒霉催的就倒霉在没魔改上，在最开始曝光的时候，因为莫名其妙多了个杨沂真这么个女角色，一度引起很多原著粉丝不满，毕竟《绍宋》是一部大男主的故事，国仇家恨的大时代哪有时间谈恋爱啊，结果等我真玩到本作，发现本作真没有什么恋爱剧情，这些内容都被藏进了边边角角里，要是你不收集基本都看不到，看得出导演和投资方对《绍宋》这个IP还是挺重视的，但也因此导致《绍宋》这款游戏极度的“小说化”。
很多内容你读小说还好，毕竟一目十行嘛，但你要是看他们表演出来，就会发现太冗长了，整款游戏播片部分几乎全部都是文戏，这种内容看小说非常爽但看人演就非常的煎熬，归根结底互动影游这个游戏形式更类似短剧，就要不断的出现爆点，而《绍宋》原著是一本长篇网文，厚积才能薄发，这就导致即便导演组已经尽全力删改了，用影视呈现出来的效果依旧是差强人意。
这也引出了游戏的第二个致命性问题——长篇故事和短剧的不兼容，因为游戏基本上是完全按照《绍宋》原著演的，《绍宋》这个小说完全是可以改编成大型连视剧的，但是制作组不可能按照电视剧架构去拍，这就导致观影体验极度的别扭，换句话说，这就好像一部长篇电视剧被剪辑成了四个小时的短剧，看着很多地方都很敷衍糊弄，而另一些部分又过分的无聊，往好处想这样最起码满足了原著粉……吗？
很不幸，这游戏也没有满足原著粉，原著粉想看什么，很明显就是战争戏，决战八公山也好，龙纛前压也罢，这些文字转化成影视都需要海量的资金，而游戏制作组肉眼可见的贫穷，既然如此那就用AI来生成战争画面，再搭配真人实拍的近景镜头。
制作组绝对觉得自己是个天才，对吧？
但是呢，现在的AI什么水平懂的都懂，太劣质了，这种劣质的AI极大地影响了玩家的观影体验，对于原著粉来说，你都搞不好基础的战争，那你不如不拿这个IP，弄得里外不是人——影游玩家觉得无聊，原著粉觉得敷衍。
更雪上加霜的是制作组还在搞花活，似乎是意识到自己这个所谓的“游戏”本质上就是一条线到底，为了增加更多互动要素，本作引入了战棋玩法。
但你既然搞战棋，你就给我搞好了呀！
你搞得什么东西，3A大作是吧？
AI画图、AI语音、AI设计
这么低劣的战棋甚至进一步拖垮了游戏的节奏，都2026年了，你能想象一个战棋没有绕背、没有侧击，主要关卡都是逃亡战——跑了就是胜利。
这么低劣的战棋不如不制作，最起码能降低玩家的观影成本，制作组也意识到了这一点，直接设计了战棋游戏可以跳过，这就让本作的战棋更加尴尬了——既然你可以跳过，你为什么要加入这个东西呢？
就这个战棋完全没有意义，有些游戏战棋胜利了可以影响播片剧情，而你这个玩意毫无影响啊，哥们。
你要是这么不自信，你为什么要设计这个战棋，而更让我绷不住的是，游戏的战棋设计似乎和剧组是完全脱节的，举个例子，游戏第五章韩常都被刘晏杀了，那段戏搞得还挺激烈的，韩常死前还放狠话呢，结果一转头到战棋里，诶，韩常复活了，神不神奇、意不意外、吃不吃惊、惊不惊喜，大金死灵法术你值得拥有。
两个游戏模式完全脱节，这让我真的很难想象这是一款发售的游戏，而不是测试的DEMO，这体现出来项目管理的极端草台班子化，好钢没用到刀刃上，有那个成本搞这种垃圾战棋，为什么不多拍几条分支路线？
如果了解这个制作组，就应该知道，去年这个组搞了个《明末：伐定天下》，不吹不黑，《绍宋：还我河山》确实比《伐定天下》在表演上靠谱多了，《伐定天下》里面充斥着太多古早网文时代让人尴尬的桥段，从这一点看，《绍宋》的文本确实更踏实——虽然跟李清照接触的那几段戏还是挺尴尬的。
但是，你跟去年的自己比进步了，不代表你这个游戏在互动影游这个分类里真的算特别出众，游戏几个演员的表现，客观来说演的很卖力但真的演的不好。
首先就是主角赵玖的扮演者“银城武”徐越，徐越这个演员去年因为《情感反诈模拟器》的神级表演火了一把，今年演赵玖，我只能说他很努力了，但各方面都不太合格，首先徐越年龄不小了，他更适合演那种痞帅的成熟男人，而不是那种大学生小白，这就导致他在游戏开头那一幕的表现几乎是灾难性的，油腻的老登装嫩的感觉，类似2006年版《神雕侠侣》黄晓明表演的前期杨过，这人物感觉就不对味，作为玩家你能感觉到徐越尽力了，但他各种出戏，服化道也没有体现出徐越的优势区间，反而让徐越的赵玖差了点意思。
而另一个明星演员就是王涵，关于这位女演员，粉丝很多，但客观来说，她在游戏里戏份不算多，而且化的妆也挺一言难尽的，我就记得她在《美女，请别影响我成仙》里面的样子还是挺好看的，怎么一到这游戏服化道就这么别扭呢，属于是天生丽质也扳不过来的程度，尤其是那个刘海怎么看怎么难受。
另外还有一位值得一提的大牌就是左小青，互动影游能请来这么老资历的演员还是挺惊喜的，左小青的气质和年龄扮演李清照都是合适的，问题是似乎是制作组没多少钱，导致左小青的戏份没几场，完全沦为彩蛋人物，让人颇为遗憾。
至于其他的演员基本都是《明末：伐定天下》的熟面孔了，也是万维猫的那批演员，扮演岳飞的张晓晨也算是半个熟面孔，上半年大火的历史剧《太平年》里面他演李元清，说心里话，他演的岳飞很敷衍，主要是演员自身条件和岳飞的气质差了不少，不够魁梧挺拔，看起来也稍微有些阴郁算计，总觉得不够光明磊落，当然这就是个人观感了。
这款游戏在发售前，给人的感觉应该是今年互动影游NO.1，毕竟导演是《江山北望》的导演，演员又是从各大知名影游和长剧拉来的，再加上《绍宋》这么一个稳赚不赔的超级IP，结果搞成这个样子，真的让人扼腕叹息。
归根结底，我觉得还是万维猫步子太大了，完全没考虑自己的实力，影游这个类型毕竟之前鹅厂的《盛世天下》抬高了档次，虽然面向受众不同，但玩家的审美也被养刁了，而你这么个绍宋肉眼可见的缺钱，说白了，比起那些恋爱影游，《绍宋》的规格是很高的，但你的竞争对手从来不是这些满足宅男幻想的作品，你的对手是第一档次那批影游，在这种情况下，在没有那么多钱的前提下搞《绍宋》这个IP就是自不量力。
事实上，去年这款游戏刚放出预告片的时候，很多玩家就质疑制作组能不能把《绍宋》的大场面呈现好，结果今年端上来这么一个AI大场面预制菜，真的对不起玩家的信任啊。
这游戏要是单纯当成短剧来看，效果还是不错的，可最搞笑乃至于让人绷不住的正是这一点——他作为一款游戏，只有被人当成短剧的时候才能算是不错

先说结论：如果你是《绍宋》原著党、历史题材爱好者，或者喜欢真人互动影游，这部我建议直接玩。
但如果你期待的是一款真正意义上的大型历史策略游戏，那我反而建议你先降低预期。因为《绍宋：还我河山》最容易被吐槽的地方，其实也是它最容易被误解的地方——它本质上首先是一部“真人互动历史剧”，其次才是游戏。战棋、QTE、选择分支这些东西，说到底都是在服务剧情。
        所以别指望它能和正儿八经的策略游戏比系统深度，也别指望每一个选项都能产生《底特律：变人》那种天翻地覆的蝴蝶效应。如果用这个标准去审判它，确实能挑出不少问题。但如果你接受它的定位，会发现这游戏真正有意思的地方来了。它让我第一次真正产生了“我来当赵构”的感觉。
        靖康之后，北宋已经没了。中原沦陷。金兵南下。朝堂上有人主战，有人求和，有人想着南迁，有人只想保住自己的荣华富贵。而你偏偏坐到了那个最要命的位置上。你不是在选择“剧情 A”还是“剧情 B”。你是在决定：这个天下，到底要不要继续打。这才是《绍宋》最吸引我的地方。有时候你做出一个选择，当下看起来完全没问题。过了一段剧情再回头看，才发现自己当时做的决定，已经悄悄改变了后面的局势。那种“蝴蝶效应”未必每次都非常夸张，但对于互动影游来说，已经足够让我产生继续探索其他路线的动力。
     而且我必须说一句：这游戏的真人部分，比我预想中好。当然，它不是电视剧。演员的某些表演、个别台词、部分镜头调度，依然能看出真人互动影游和传统影视作品之间的差距。这些问题确实存在。但你真正进入剧情以后，朝堂戏、人物关系、战争戏连起来，还是能慢慢把人带进去。
        尤其当你已经知道某些历史人物最终可能会走向什么结局时，再看着游戏里的角色站在你面前，会产生一种很奇妙的感觉：我知道历史本来应该怎么走。但现在，我偏偏想让它换一种走法。这才是《绍宋》最有价值的地方。
        至于 AI 素材，我觉得也没必要装看不见。官方已经明确披露部分动画、角色头像以及技能/物品图标存在 AI 生成内容。
确实会有一些地方显得不够统一。但对我来说，这属于制作层面的瑕疵，而不是直接摧毁游戏核心体验的问题。真正决定这部作品好不好玩的，还是：故事能不能让我继续看下去，选择能不能让我产生代入感。
        而这两点，《绍宋》做到了。还有一点我觉得必须说清楚：别把它当《全面战争》，也别把它当历史模拟器。官方自己都已经说明，本作是根据榴弹怕水的《绍宋》改编，剧情、历史脉络与故事走向属于虚构演绎。所以它真正卖的不是“还原历史”。而是：给你一次重新选择历史的机会。我甚至觉得这句话比“真人互动影游”更准确。因为当你坐在赵构的位置上，看着靖康之后的山河，然后做出“北伐”那个选择的时候，爽点根本不在于战棋赢了一局。而在于：这一次，历史是我选的。
        当然，如果让我挑毛病，我也能挑出一堆。玩法还不够深。部分互动略显形式化。个别演出有影游常见的尴尬感。某些地方节奏也确实会让人觉得拖。甚至部分素材的质感还有提升空间。但问题是——我还是想把它玩下去。对于一部互动影游来说，这已经可以了。因为真正差的影游，是让我恨不得赶紧跳过剧情。而《绍宋》是让我玩完一段以后，开始琢磨：“如果刚才我选另一个，会怎么样？”然后重新开一遍。这就是它真正让我上头的地方。最后《绍宋：还我河山》让我看到了一件很有意思的事情：原来“历史题材 + 真人影视 + 互动选择 + 轻策略玩法”，真的可以成立。它当然不完美。甚至有些地方还挺粗糙。
        但它敢把《绍宋》这种题材真正做成游戏，而不是简单拍一部电视剧让你偶尔点两下屏幕，这一点我愿意给它很高的评价。宋可亡，天下不可亡。以前这句话是小说里的台词。这次轮到我坐在赵构的位置上。那就让我自己来选一次。

《绍宋：还我河山》——此座可惜
在聊这款游戏之前，我想聊个历史典故，西晋开国皇帝司马炎的太子司马衷有智力障碍，当时的大臣看在眼里急在心里，尚书令卫瓘有一次喝多了就抚摸着皇位感慨“此座可惜”，司马炎也看在眼里，最后敷衍了一句说卫瓘喝多了，等到司马炎死后，司马衷登基之后，西晋的国祚也就没几天了。
为什么要聊这个呢，因为对于这款游戏和这段历史，我的评价就是“此座可惜”——用最好的IP做出来的中庸之作。
首先要承认，这款游戏真的没有魔改太多，但这游戏倒霉催的就倒霉在没魔改上，在最开始曝光的时候，因为莫名其妙多了个杨沂真这么个女角色，一度引起很多原著粉丝不满，毕竟《绍宋》是一部大男主的故事，国仇家恨的大时代哪有时间谈恋爱啊，结果等我真玩到本作，发现本作真没有什么恋爱剧情，这些内容都被藏进了边边角角里，要是你不收集基本都看不到，看得出导演和投资方对《绍宋》这个IP还是挺重视的，但也因此导致《绍宋》这款游戏极度的“小说化”。
很多内容你读小说还好，毕竟一目十行嘛，但你要是看他们表演出来，就会发现太冗长了，整款游戏播片部分几乎全部都是文戏，这种内容看小说非常爽但看人演就非常的煎熬，归根结底互动影游这个游戏形式更类似短剧，就要不断的出现爆点，而《绍宋》原著是一本长篇网文，厚积才能薄发，这就导致即便导演组已经尽全力删改了，用影视呈现出来的效果依旧是差强人意。
这也引出了游戏的第二个致命性问题——长篇故事和短剧的不兼容，因为游戏基本上是完全按照《绍宋》原著演的，《绍宋》这个小说完全是可以改编成大型连视剧的，但是制作组不可能按照电视剧架构去拍，这就导致观影体验极度的别扭，换句话说，这就好像一部长篇电视剧被剪辑成了四个小时的短剧，看着很多地方都很敷衍糊弄，而另一些部分又过分的无聊，往好处想这样最起码满足了原著粉……吗？
很不幸，这游戏也没有满足原著粉，原著粉想看什么，很明显就是战争戏，决战八公山也好，龙纛前压也罢，这些文字转化成影视都需要海量的资金，而游戏制作组肉眼可见的贫穷，既然如此那就用AI来生成战争画面，再搭配真人实拍的近景镜头。
制作组绝对觉得自己是个天才，对吧？
但是呢，现在的AI什么水平懂的都懂，太劣质了，这种劣质的AI极大地影响了玩家的观影体验，对于原著粉来说，你都搞不好基础的战争，那你不如不拿这个IP，弄得里外不是人——影游玩家觉得无聊，原著粉觉得敷衍。
更雪上加霜的是制作组还在搞花活，似乎是意识到自己这个所谓的“游戏”本质上就是一条线到底，为了增加更多互动要素，本作引入了战棋玩法。
但你既然搞战棋，你就给我搞好了呀！
你搞得什么东西，3A大作是吧？
AI画图、AI语音、AI设计
这么低劣的战棋甚至进一步拖垮了游戏的节奏，都2026年了，你能想象一个战棋没有绕背、没有侧击，主要关卡都是逃亡战——跑了就是胜利。
这么低劣的战棋不如不制作，最起码能降低玩家的观影成本，制作组也意识到了这一点，直接设计了战棋游戏可以跳过，这就让本作的战棋更加尴尬了——既然你可以跳过，你为什么要加入这个东西呢？
就这个战棋完全没有意义，有些游戏战棋胜利了可以影响播片剧情，而你这个玩意毫无影响啊，哥们。
你要是这么不自信，你为什么要设计这个战棋，而更让我绷不住的是，游戏的战棋设计似乎和剧组是完全脱节的，举个例子，游戏第五章韩常都被刘晏杀了，那段戏搞得还挺激烈的，韩常死前还放狠话呢，结果一转头到战棋里，诶，韩常复活了，神不神奇、意不意外、吃不吃惊、惊不惊喜，大金死灵法术你值得拥有。
两个游戏模式完全脱节，这让我真的很难想象这是一款发售的游戏，而不是测试的DEMO，这体现出来项目管理的极端草台班子化，好钢没用到刀刃上，有那个成本搞这种垃圾战棋，为什么不多拍几条分支路线？
如果了解这个制作组，就应该知道，去年这个组搞了个《明末：伐定天下》，不吹不黑，《绍宋：还我河山》确实比《伐定天下》在表演上靠谱多了，《伐定天下》里面充斥着太多古早网文时代让人尴尬的桥段，从这一点看，《绍宋》的文本确实更踏实——虽然跟李清照接触的那几段戏还是挺尴尬的。
但是，你跟去年的自己比进步了，不代表你这个游戏在互动影游这个分类里真的算特别出众，游戏几个演员的表现，客观来说演的很卖力但真的演的不好。
首先就是主角赵玖的扮演者“银城武”徐越，徐越这个演员去年因为《情感反诈模拟器》的神级表演火了一把，今年演赵玖，我只能说他很努力了，但各方面都不太合格，首先徐越年龄不小了，他更适合演那种痞帅的成熟男人，而不是那种大学生小白，这就导致他在游戏开头那一幕的表现几乎是灾难性的，油腻的老登装嫩的感觉，类似2006年版《神雕侠侣》黄晓明表演的前期杨过，这人物感觉就不对味，作为玩家你能感觉到徐越尽力了，但他各种出戏，服化道也没有体现出徐越的优势区间，反而让徐越的赵玖差了点意思。
而另一个明星演员就是王涵，关于这位女演员，粉丝很多，但客观来说，她在游戏里戏份不算多，而且化的妆也挺一言难尽的，我就记得她在《美女，请别影响我成仙》里面的样子还是挺好看的，怎么一到这游戏服化道就这么别扭呢，属于是天生丽质也扳不过来的程度，尤其是那个刘海怎么看怎么难受。
另外还有一位值得一提的大牌就是左小青，互动影游能请来这么老资历的演员还是挺惊喜的，左小青的气质和年龄扮演李清照都是合适的，问题是似乎是制作组没多少钱，导致左小青的戏份没几场，完全沦为彩蛋人物，让人颇为遗憾。
至于其他的演员基本都是《明末：伐定天下》的熟面孔了，也是万维猫的那批演员，扮演岳飞的张晓晨也算是半个熟面孔，上半年大火的历史剧《太平年》里面他演李元清，说心里话，他演的岳飞很敷衍，主要是演员自身条件和岳飞的气质差了不少，不够魁梧挺拔，看起来也稍微有些阴郁算计，总觉得不够光明磊落，当然这就是个人观感了。
这款游戏在发售前，给人的感觉应该是今年互动影游NO.1，毕竟导演是《江山北望》的导演，演员又是从各大知名影游和长剧拉来的，再加上《绍宋》这么一个稳赚不赔的超级IP，结果搞成这个样子，真的让人扼腕叹息。
归根结底，我觉得还是万维猫步子太大了，完全没考虑自己的实力，影游这个类型毕竟之前鹅厂的《盛世天下》抬高了档次，虽然面向受众不同，但玩家的审美也被养刁了，而你这么个绍宋肉眼可见的缺钱，说白了，比起那些恋爱影游，《绍宋》的规格是很高的，但你的竞争对手从来不是这些满足宅男幻想的作品，你的对手是第一档次那批影游，在这种情况下，在没有那么多钱的前提下搞《绍宋》这个IP就是自不量力。
事实上，去年这款游戏刚放出预告片的时候，很多玩家就质疑制作组能不能把《绍宋》的大场面呈现好，结果今年端上来这么一个AI大场面预制菜，真的对不起玩家的信任啊。
这游戏要是单纯当成短剧来看，效果还是不错的，可最搞笑乃至于让人绷不住的正是这一点——他作为一款游戏，只有被人当成短剧的时候才能算是不错

所以我才在一开始说这款游戏叫“此座可惜”，天子的位置啊，栓条狗上去你都能躺着挣钱吧，结果呢，因为自身的不自量力，游戏的成品质量让人大跌眼镜。

卖垃圾送游戏，商家一群狗东西。好好的题材、硬是能被制作组做成一坨狗屎，属于是拿着现成的好牌都能打得稀烂。

先不说内容，光进个游戏就折腾半天，流程和技术水平烂得让人怀疑到底有没有认真测试过。好不容易进去了，又开始疯狂闪屏，晃得人眼睛都快瞎了。2026年了还能做出这种完成度，我也是第一次见。

最可惜的是原本这么好的题材，被这种制作水平白白浪费。建议制作组少想着靠原作情怀割韭菜，先把最基本的技术、优化和用户体验做好。不会做就回去重新学，别拿着别人的好作品出来糟蹋，更别让消费者花钱帮你们测试半成品。
游戏频闪，语音顿挫，章节名全部显示一样进度100%，无法点击，无法正常游玩，反映了三天了，这样的恶性bug都没处理，网上也找到有人遇到了同样的问题，显示游玩两个小时全在想办法解决问题，折腾了几天就看见了康履派人杀赵九，我连评价内容都没法评价，这逼游戏厂商真是见过最垃圾的，想赚钱至少得让游戏正常运行吧

在我心里绍宋已经是互动影游的NO.1了，主要是剧情很棒，选在南宋初期，太有代入感了。而且我没看过小说，就当看剧根本停不下来。隔壁李唐的历史人物都要改名换姓，绍宋就大大方方用历史原型，这点十分好评。
战棋游戏其实很鸡肋，好在可以跳过，无伤大雅。有些场景用了AI问题不大，毕竟实拍太烧经费，而且占比也不高。这种涉及战争布局的会给地图详情这点很棒，一目了然看得很舒服。
希望快点出下一部！！！

先说结论：不推荐购买。但我仍然给了好评。

作为影游爱好者，我极少给这类作品打差评，尤其对古风题材始终抱有一份偏爱，更何况在当下，愿意做古风影游的团队已经越来越少。但坦白说，玩到中后期时，我已经开始边挂机边刷手机了，连约会事件都不想再点了，只想尽快推完主线，卸载了事。

先谈所谓的“模拟经营”系统。它完全是个噱头，删掉它对游戏流程没有任何影响，存在与否毫无区别。

成就系统则完全是结局导向的：有多少个成就，就意味着有多少个结局。而问题在于，流程冗长到目前网上连一份完整的攻略都凑不出来，全成就的动力被消磨得所剩无几。

人物方面，能明显看出《咸鱼殿下》的影子，但服化道辨识度极低，角色之间大同小异。人物塑造甚至不如《完蛋 2》，通关后我记不住任何一个角色的鲜明个性。也就钱思怡因为算是“老面孔”而稍有印象。也有人会提到庄晓曼的客串，反差感确实让人意外，我第一眼也没认出来。但说实话，她和那位初看名字被我误认为“宋妍飞”的角色，在定位上几乎重叠，我不太理解为什么要设计两个如此相似的人物。

角色塑造让人记不住就算了。某些角色“公主”，你自己看看你说她是公主你信吗？非洲部落的土著公主也没这么难看吧？选角导演眉毛底下那两个窟窿眼是出气的吗？

剧情方面，体量大、支线杂，碎片化严重。约会剧情与主线经常脱节，明明角色已被派出任务，点一下约会界面，他又突然出现在你面前，时空逻辑完全不顾。更让人失望的是大量纯文字叙述，连配音都没有，后期主线也充斥着这类“PPT式”推进。这也是我最终放弃、开始刷手机的根本原因，因为实在看不进去了。

再说叙事结构。传统影游大多靠故事线分支推进，本作虽然也有类似设计，却额外塞入了一套存读档系统。主线结局必须靠存档、读档来切换，而非主线的分支则仍走故事线。说实话，我真没搞懂这套混合逻辑的用意。如果你玩过《美女》系列、《你好》系列或者黑岩家的作品，就会明白那种故事线做得有多顺畅——第一章改一个选项，可以直接跳到最后一章触发结局，根本不需要从头再点一遍。而本作加了存读档，剧情又拖得极长，反倒成了劝退全成就的最大障碍。

我是真的很少给影游差评，但这部作品在我这儿只能排“NPC”。不过，我还是给了好评，毕竟这是新团队的首作，也毕竟他们还愿意押注古风这一在影游圈日渐小众的赛道。这份勇气值得鼓励。但若你问我是否推荐新人入手，我的答案是否定的。不好玩，就是最直接的理由。
